question:
A technician is troubleshooting an all-in-one laser printer that prints a vertical line when making copies and scans. When users print or receive
 faxes, the output from the printer is correct. Which of the following should the technician examine to determine the cause of the issue?
explanation: Copies and scans are the only jobs that travel through the scanning path, and both are affected while printed and received faxes are clean, so the fault is on the document feeder side - debris or a scratch on the narrow ADF scan strip draws the same line down every sheet pulled past it. D (The drum assembly) and B (The corona wire) live in the print engine, so defects there would mark faxes and normal prints too. A (The pickup rollers) cause misfeeds and jams, not lines. (Note: the dump prints D as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says C — we go with the community.)

question: Which of the following is an advantage of using a hybrid cloud instead of a public cloud?

options.C: Ability to meet data residency requirements
options.D: Ability to leverage IaaS and PaaS

explanation: Hybrid lets an organization keep regulated data on private, on-premises infrastructure it physically controls while still bursting other workloads into the public cloud, which is how data residency and sovereignty rules are satisfied. A (Ability to reduce management overhead) points the other way - hybrid means running and integrating two environments. D (Ability to leverage IaaS and PaaS) is available in a plain public cloud as well, and B (Ability to use cross-platform virtualization) is a hypervisor capability, not a cloud deployment model benefit.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting a desktop PC that is plugged into a UPS. The PC loses the system date/time after every power outage. Which of
 the following should the technician do to resolve the issue? (Choose two.)
explanation: E (Replace the CMOS battery) fixes the clock itself: the coin cell keeps the real-time clock and BIOS settings alive whenever the board has no AC power, and losing date/time each time the system goes dark is the classic dead-battery symptom. D (Repair the backup power source) explains why the board is going dark at all - a working UPS should carry the PC through the outage instead of letting it drop. A (Run a BIOS update) and B (Swap out the RAM) have no bearing on timekeeping.

question:
A network administrator must ensure that a printer will still be assigned a specific IP address even if all addresses are depleted. Which of the
 following network configuration concepts is this describing?
explanation: A DHCP reservation binds a chosen address to the printer's MAC address, so the server always hands that same IP back to it and holds it aside even when the rest of the scope is fully leased. D (Exclusion) pulls an address out of the pool so that nobody is assigned it dynamically - it is not tied to a device. B (Lease) is just the time-limited grant of any pool address, and A (VLAN) is layer 2 segmentation, unrelated to address assignment.

question:
A user is having issues when charging a device with a Lightning cable. The cable is not recognized when it is plugged into the device. This issue is
 usually resolved by flipping the cable over. This issue does not occur with other devices of the same type. Which of the following would most
 likely cause the issue?

options.A: The device needs to be restarted.
options.B: The battery may be swelling and needs inspection.
options.C: The cable is failing and needs to be replaced.
options.D: The charging port is dirty or damaged

explanation: Lightning connectors are reversible with contacts on both faces, so if flipping the cable makes it work, one row of pins inside the device's port is dirty, bent or corroded. C (The cable is failing) is ruled out because the same cable works on other devices of the same type. A (Restart the device) cannot explain an orientation-dependent connection, and B (Swelling battery) shows up as a bulging case or lifted display. (Note: the dump prints C as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says D — we go with the community.)

question: Which of the following servers is used to collect data and information about events from a network-connected host?
explanation: A syslog server is the standard collection point for event and log messages pushed from hosts, routers, switches and firewalls, normally over UDP 514, giving one place to search and correlate activity. A (DNS) resolves names to IP addresses, B (Mail) handles message delivery with SMTP, POP3 and IMAP, and C (Print) queues and spools jobs to printers. None of those aggregate event data from other network devices.

question: A technician observes slow startup times on a laptop. Which of the following is most likely causing the issue?
explanation: Booting means loading the operating system and all startup programs from storage into memory, and a mechanical hard drive's seek times and low transfer rate make that the slowest link - swapping in an SSD is the standard fix. B (RAM) shortages show as sluggish multitasking and heavy paging once the system is running rather than a slow boot. C (NIC) only affects network throughput, and D (BIOS) firmware only accounts for the brief POST phase before the OS begins loading.

question:
A customer reports their tablet was recently dropped on the ground. The tablet has a small crack in one corner of the display, and it does not
 charge when plugged in. Which of the following should a technician do first?

options.C: Inspect the USB-C port for damage.

explanation: The device took physical damage and now will not charge, so the first step is the cheapest, least invasive one: look into the USB-C port for bent pins, debris or a cracked housing before replacing anything. B (Replace the battery) swaps a part before the fault is identified, and A (Perform a hard restart) will not restore a physically broken power path. D (Run diagnostics on the digitizer) tests touch response, which is a separate symptom from the charging failure.

question: A technician needs to select PC components with a minimal number of visible internal cables. Which of the following should the technician use?
explanation: A modular power supply lets the technician attach only the power leads the build actually needs and leave the rest in the box, which is the single biggest reduction in visible cabling inside a case. A (SATA drive connections) add both a data cable and a power lead per drive, so they increase clutter. B (Liquid cooling) introduces tubing and pump wiring, and D (Wireless NIC) only removes an external network cable, not internal ones.

question:
A user is traveling internationally. They can make and receive phone calls but cannot send or receive email. Which of the following would most
 likely resolve this issue?
explanation: Voice and SMS ride the carrier's roaming agreements and often keep working abroad, but mobile data is a separate service that is disabled by default to prevent bill shock - email needs that data channel, so enabling data roaming restores it. C (Configuring 4G usage only) restricts the radio technology and does nothing about roaming permission. D (Connecting using a hotspot) is a workaround that still depends on some other data source, and A (Disabling the GPS) has no effect on connectivity.

question: Which of the following should be used when installing network cabling above a drop ceiling that is part of the shared air space?
explanation: Plenum-rated cable uses a low-smoke, flame-retardant jacket such as FEP so it will not feed a fire or release toxic fumes into circulated air, and fire codes require it in any ceiling or floor space used as a return air plenum. A (Shielded twisted) pair addresses EMI and RFI, which is an interference concern rather than a fire code one. C (Optical) and D (Coaxial) are cable media choices that still need a plenum-rated jacket in that space, so neither answers the requirement.

question:
While using a computer, a user reports that the system fan begins running loudly and the display starts to distort. Which of the following is
 occurring?
explanation: Fans ramping loudly means the thermal sensors are seeing high temperatures, and a hot GPU or CPU producing artifacts and distortion on screen is the classic pairing - the cause is overheating from blocked airflow, dust or dried thermal paste. B (Sluggish performance) and D (Crashing applications) are symptoms that overheating can eventually produce, not the underlying condition being described. C (Overclocking CPU) is something a user deliberately configures, and nothing here indicates the clocks were raised.

question: Which of the following is a common feature of managed switches?
explanation: Managed switches expose a configuration interface, and assigning ports to VLANs is the defining feature - it lets an administrator split one physical switch into separate broadcast domains for security and traffic control, which an unmanaged switch cannot do. A (Remote device power delivery) is PoE, available on plenty of unmanaged switches as a hardware feature. C (Content filtering) belongs to a firewall or proxy, and D (Load balancing) is handled by a dedicated appliance or layer 4-7 device.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of Type 2 hypervisors?
explanation: A Type 2, or hosted, hypervisor such as VirtualBox or VMware Workstation installs as an application on top of an existing Windows, macOS or Linux install and reaches hardware through that host OS. A (Bare-metal installation) describes a Type 1 hypervisor, which runs directly on the hardware with no host OS beneath it. D (Specific hardware requirements) also fits Type 1, which is tied to a hardware compatibility list, and C (Local management only) is untrue - hosted hypervisors can be managed remotely.

question: Which of the following port numbers is used for a file transfer?
explanation: FTP uses TCP 21 as its control channel for logins and commands, with data moving on port 20 or a negotiated passive port, making 21 the file transfer answer. B (53) is DNS name resolution, C (68) is the DHCP client port that receives offers from the server on 67, and D (389) is LDAP directory lookups. None of those move files.

question:
A user wants to print files from an overseas office using a shared network folder The user's laptop has no public-facing internet connectivity.
 Which of the following can be used to print from the shared network folder?
explanation: SMB is the Windows file and printer sharing protocol, running over TCP 445 on the internal network, so the laptop can reach the shared folder and the shared print queue without any public internet connectivity. A (ADF) is the automatic document feeder on a scanner, hardware rather than a protocol. C (PCL) is the page description language the job is rendered in once it reaches the printer, and B (USB) is a direct local connection that cannot span an overseas office.

question:
A user tries to connect a monitor to a laptop to have an additional screen for work, but both screens show the same content. Which of the
 following should the user do to resolve the issue?

options.A: Use the Add New Hardware assistant to add the monitor and set up the required settings.
options.B: Purchase a docking station to connect both the laptop and the monitor.
options.C: Configure the Windows tiling feature to display multiple windows.
options.D: Go to the Display settings and configure the external monitor as extended.

explanation: Windows defaults to duplicating the desktop on a newly attached display, so opening Display settings and switching the second monitor to Extend gives the separate working area the user wants. A (Use the Add New Hardware assistant) applies to a device that was never detected, and this monitor is clearly detected since it is mirroring. B (Purchase a docking station) spends money on hardware that is already working, and C (Configure the Windows tiling feature) just arranges windows within a screen.

question: Which of the following best represents the purpose of NFC?

options.B: Short-distance wireless connections between two devices
options.C: Wireless connections between multiple devices at once
options.D: Direct connection of two computers for file sharing

explanation: NFC works only at a few centimetres between two devices, which is what makes it safe for tap-to-pay, transit cards, badge tags and quick Bluetooth pairing handoffs. C (Wireless connections between multiple devices at once) fits Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, which serve several peers over much greater distance. D (Direct connection of two computers for file sharing) describes Wi-Fi Direct or an ad hoc link, and A (Wired connections between several devices) is not wireless at all.

question:
A group of friends is gathering in a room to play video games. One of the friends has a game server. Which of the following network types should
 the group use so they can all connect to the same server and the internet?
explanation: Everyone is in one room sharing a single router and switch, which is the textbook definition of a LAN - it lets all the clients reach the local game server and still route out to the internet. D (PAN) is a personal-range network like Bluetooth, covering roughly ten metres between a person's own devices, and it does not provide internet access to a group. B (MAN) spans a city, and A (SAN) is a dedicated block storage network, not a general purpose one.

question: Which of the following can a user utilize to share their mobile phone connection with their laptop?
explanation: Tethering makes the phone act as a modem for the laptop, sharing the cellular data connection over USB, Bluetooth or a Wi-Fi hotspot. C (Wi-Fi Direct) creates a peer-to-peer link for transferring files or printing between devices, not for sharing an upstream internet connection. B (NFC) works only over a few centimetres for payments and pairing, and A (IR) is legacy, line-of-sight, and far too slow to carry a network connection.

question: A user reports that their desktop PC does not turn on. Which of the following components would most likely cause the issue?
explanation: The power supply converts wall AC to the DC rails every other component needs, so a dead PSU means the board never gets voltage, no POST occurs and nothing at all happens when the button is pressed. B (GPU) failure still lets fans spin and the system power on, just with no video. C (RAM) failure typically produces beep codes or a blank POST with the system clearly powered, and D (CPU) failure likewise still shows signs of power being applied.

question: The printer in a main office repeatedly jams. Which of the following tasks should a support technician do to solve the issue?
explanation: Repeated jams point at worn paper-path parts, and a laser printer maintenance kit bundles exactly those consumables - pickup rollers, separation pad, transfer roller and fuser - so fitting one and resetting the page counter is the correct fix. B (Replace toner or ink cartridges) addresses print quality such as faded or streaky output, not paper feed. C (Install a new ribbon) applies to impact printers, and D (Change the printhead) applies to inkjets.

question:
A technician is installing a new printer. After registering the printer, the technician receives an email from the manufacturer stating there is a
 security vulnerability that can be remediated. Which of the following steps should the technician take next?

options.D: Disable the default gateway on the printer.

explanation: When a vendor announces a remediable vulnerability, they have released a patched firmware image, so flashing the printer's firmware is the step that actually closes the hole. A (Disable wireless connectivity) removes a feature the customer paid for while leaving the flaw present on the wired interface. B (Enable audit logging) records activity but fixes nothing, and D (Disable the default gateway on the printer) simply breaks routed printing and management traffic.

question:
A technician has built a new computer. On the initial startup, the computer passes POST but will not turn on the operating system. Which of the
 following components has failed?
explanation: Passing POST proves the CPU, RAM, power delivery and board initialized correctly, so the failure is at the handoff to the boot device - a hard drive that is unplugged, unformatted, has no OS installed or has failed. C (Power supply) trouble would prevent POST from completing at all. B (CPU) failure means no POST either, and A (Audio card) plays no part in the boot process.

question:
A user reports slow internet browsing. The technician finds high CPU and memory usage, and pop-ups occur every minute. Which of the following
 should the technician do next?

options.A: Escalate to the network team to check end-to-end connectivity.
options.B: Download and install the latest drivers.
options.C: Update the anti-malware signatures and scan the system.
options.D: Check the wireless settings and validate the DHCP configuration.

explanation: Constant pop-ups combined with pegged CPU and memory are hallmark adware or malware behaviour, so the next step is updating the anti-malware definitions and running a full scan, which is where the malware removal process begins once symptoms are identified. A (Escalate to the network team) is premature when the evidence is entirely local to this machine. B (Download and install the latest drivers) does not generate or cure pop-ups, and D (Check the wireless settings and validate the DHCP configuration) cannot explain the resource consumption.

question: Which of the following is the best to use when testing a file for potential malware?
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated, disposable environment where a suspect file can be detonated and observed with no path back to the host or the production network, and it can be reverted afterwards. C (Cross-platform virtualization) merely describes running one OS on another and offers no isolation guarantee by itself. A (Multitenancy) is multiple customers sharing cloud infrastructure, and B (Test development) is a software lifecycle stage, not a containment method.

question: Which of the following resolutions is commonly known as Ultra HD?
explanation: Ultra HD is the consumer standard at 3840x2160, four times the pixel count of 1080p and the resolution marketed on 4K televisions and monitors. A (1920x1080) is Full HD, and D (7680x4320) is 8K, or Full Ultra HD. B (2048x1080) is DCI 2K, the cinema format - note that true DCI 4K is 4096x2160, slightly wider than UHD, which is why 3840x2160 is the precise answer here.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting stylus issues on identical company-provided tablets. Users can purchase their own accessories. Some users have
 no issues, but others report that their styluses charge intermittently and die frequently. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this
 issue?

options.A: Certain cases are causing charging issues.
options.B: The tablets need to be updated.
options.C: Some of the tablets have manufacturing defects.
options.D: The malfunctioning styluses need firmware updates.

explanation: The tablets are identical company issue and some users have no trouble, so the variable is the accessory each person chose; styluses charge magnetically or inductively against a specific spot on the tablet, and a thick or ill-fitting third-party case holds the stylus off that contact point so it charges only intermittently. C (Manufacturing defects) is unlikely across identical units where many work perfectly. B (The tablets need to be updated) and D (Firmware updates) would affect the whole fleet equally, not a subset defined by accessory choice.

question:
A user prints a job from a laser printer. The user wipes the page, and the words and images come off of it. The technician replaces the toner
 cartridge, but the issue persists. Which of the following components should the technician replace next?
explanation: The fuser applies heat and pressure to melt toner permanently into the paper fibres; if the print wipes off, the toner was laid down but never fused, so a failed fuser assembly is the part to replace. B (Drum) faults cause repeating spots, ghosting or lines rather than loose toner. C (Developer roller) problems produce faded or blank output because too little toner reaches the drum, and D (Discharge lamp) failure causes ghosting from residual charge.

question: Which of the following has the best penetration through physical objects, such as walls?
explanation: 2.4GHz has the longest wavelength of the Wi-Fi bands, so it diffracts and passes through drywall, doors and floors with the least attenuation, trading throughput for range. B (5GHz) and C (6GHz) carry far more bandwidth on wider channels but are absorbed much more heavily by building materials, with 6GHz the worst of the three. D (NFC) works over a few centimetres and is not a Wi-Fi band at all.

question: Which of the following is a Bluetooth network an example of?
explanation: Bluetooth is the standard for wireless personal area networks - short range, roughly ten metres, linking one person's headset, keyboard, watch or car kit. B (LAN) covers a building or office floor over Ethernet and Wi-Fi, a much larger scope with routed internet access. C (WAN) links sites across cities or countries, and D (SAN) is a dedicated high-speed network presenting block storage to servers.

question: Which of the following cloud models would multiple organizations in the same industry most likely use?
explanation: A community cloud is shared infrastructure built for several organizations with the same mission, regulatory burden or security requirements - healthcare providers or government agencies pooling resources and cost while keeping outsiders off the platform. A (Public) is open to any paying customer with no shared compliance posture. D (Private) serves exactly one organization, and B (Hybrid) describes mixing private and public resources within a single organization.

question: Which of the following is an example of VDI?

options.A: Streaming a GUI to thin clients from a server
options.B: Provisioning a sandbox as a test environment
options.C: Providing high-performance workstations with a local OS
options.D: Launching a virtual machine server on a hypervisor

explanation: VDI hosts each user's desktop as a virtual machine in the data center and streams only the screen, keyboard and mouse to a thin client, so compute and data stay centralized. D (Launching a virtual machine server on a hypervisor) is ordinary server virtualization with no desktop delivery layer. C (Providing high-performance workstations with a local OS) is the opposite model, with everything running locally, and B (Provisioning a sandbox) is an isolated test environment.

question: A company needs to develop a disaster recovery solution based on virtual machines. Which of the following service models is the most suitable?
explanation: IaaS supplies raw virtual machines, storage and networking on demand, which is exactly what a VM-based disaster recovery site needs - you replicate images to the provider and spin them up during a failover, paying for capacity rather than a second data center. C (Platform as a service) hands you a managed runtime and hides the VMs, so you cannot restore your own machine images to it. D (Software as a service) delivers finished applications, and B (Security as a service) provides filtering and monitoring.

question: A technician is connecting a hands-free car system via Bluetooth. Which of the following is a security feature that should be used for this task?
explanation: Bluetooth pairing is protected by a PIN or passkey that both ends must confirm, which stops a nearby attacker from pairing with the head unit and prevents accidental connections to the wrong car. A (BitLocker) is Windows full disk encryption, and C (TPM) is a chip that stores keys for a computer - neither has any role in a Bluetooth pairing exchange. B (Biometrics) authenticates a person to a device, not one device to another.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting a laptop's connectivity via its USB-C port to a projector. The same laptop works well when it is connected to a USB-
 C docking station. The projector is configured as expected, and the USB-C cable was tested on a charging port. Which of the following could be
 the issue?

options.A: The USB-C cable requires a power injector
options.B: The USB-C cable is not compatible with Thunderbolt technology.
options.C: The USB-C cable needs an adapter to work with the laptop.
options.D: The USB-C cable does not support enough power.

explanation: USB-C is only a connector shape; carrying video requires DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt support in both the cable and the port, and a plain charging cable has no video lanes. The dock works because it negotiates over an alt-mode capable link, and this cable has only been proven to deliver power. D (Not enough power) and A (Power injector) address charging, which was never the failure, and C (Needs an adapter) is wrong because the connector already fits.

question:
A high-end workstation with a RAID 5 array is exhibiting slow data access speeds and occasional errors when retrieving files. The technician
 investigates further and notices one of the hard drives in the RAID array has an amber light. Which of the following steps should the technician
 take to troubleshoot and resolve the issues?

options.A: Review network issues that might be causing slow speeds.
options.B: Upgrade all RAID drives to higher capacity models to increase data access speeds.
options.C: Replace the failing drive, and then allow the RAID controller to rebuild the array.
options.D: Reformat all drives in the RAID array to clear any software issues that might be causing the errors.

explanation: An amber drive light is the controller flagging a failed or failing member; RAID 5 keeps running in a degraded state on parity, which explains the slow reads and errors, so pulling the bad disk and letting the controller rebuild onto a replacement restores both performance and redundancy. D (Reformat all drives) destroys the array and the data. B (Upgrade all RAID drives) is expensive and ignores the actual fault, and A (Review network issues) is irrelevant to local disk access.

question: Which of the following provides electricity to devices through network cables?
explanation: A PoE switch injects DC power onto the same twisted-pair run that carries the data, so cameras, access points and VoIP phones need no local outlet. C (Access point) is normally a consumer of PoE, not a source of it. D (Patch panel) is a passive termination point with no electronics, and A (Edge router) forwards traffic between networks and does not energize the cabling.

question:
An IT specialist sets up a wireless router in a SOHO environment. Afterward, several devices cannot access the internet and are assigned IP
 addresses starting with 169.254. Which of the following is the best action to resolve this issue?
explanation: A 169.254 address means the client asked for DHCP, got no reply and fell back to APIPA; on a freshly configured SOHO router the usual cause is a DHCP service that did not start cleanly, so rebooting the router restarts it and clients pick up real leases. C (Static IP addresses) is a workaround that leaves DHCP broken. B (Shorten the lease time) and D (Increase the DHCP pool size) both assume the server is answering, which APIPA shows it is not.

question: A customer reports slow network speeds. Which of the following components is most likely failing?
explanation: The network interface card is the only listed component in the data path to the network, and a failing NIC or one that has renegotiated to a lower speed or half duplex produces exactly the slow throughput, retransmissions and errors being reported. A (CPU) and D (RAM) shortages slow the whole system rather than network transfers specifically, and C (HDD) affects file read and write times locally. Confirm by checking the link speed and the adapter's error counters.

question:
A support technician receives a call stating that a user has added a device to the network. The user used the same configurations from another
 workstation. When both workstations are turned on, neither can access the network reliably. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the
 issue?

options.A: The new computer has a duplicate IP address.
options.B: The DNS server is registering both hostnames.
options.C: The network cable was improperly terminated
options.D: The security on the switchport needs to be reset.

explanation: Copying the configuration wholesale from the other workstation copied its static IP address, so two hosts now claim the same address and both drop off intermittently as ARP entries fight - Windows also logs an address conflict. B (The DNS server is registering both hostnames) is normal behaviour and would not break connectivity for both machines. C (Improperly terminated cable) would only affect the new machine, and D (Switchport security) typically shuts one port down rather than causing both hosts to work unreliably.

question:
A technician needs to confirm that desktop PCs can be deployed to a global, remote workforce. Which of the following specifications should the
 technician validate?
explanation: Mains supply differs by country - roughly 100V in Japan, 120V in North America and 230V in much of Europe and Asia - so the technician must confirm the power supplies are auto-switching or correctly rated, otherwise the units will not run or will be damaged when plugged in. B (BIOS language support) is a convenience setting that can be changed. D (Power efficiency) is a running-cost concern, and C (Supply chain security) is a procurement issue, not a hardware specification that decides whether the PC works overseas.

question: A company deploys server machines in a public cloud. Which of the following cloud service models is this an example of?
explanation: Deploying your own server instances on a provider's virtualized hardware is IaaS: the provider owns the physical compute, storage and network, while you own the OS, patching and everything above it. A (Platform as a service) hands over a managed runtime and database so you never touch the server itself. D (Software as a service) delivers a finished application, and B (Anything as a service) is a catch-all umbrella term rather than the specific model in use.

question:
A customer needs to install a new printer in their network. The customer reports that users had intermittent connectivity issues with previous
 printers. Which of the following should the technician configure on the new printer to prevent this issue?
explanation: Intermittent printer access is the classic symptom of an address that changes when a DHCP lease expires, because workstations still have the old IP in their printer port. Assigning a static IP pins the printer to one address permanently so the queues keep working. B (DHCP IP address) is the source of the problem unless a reservation is used. A (Gateway IP address) is required for routing but is not what identifies the printer, and D (Public IP address) would expose the device directly to the internet.

question: Which of the following DNS records would an administrator change to redirect email flow?
explanation: The MX record tells sending mail servers which host accepts mail for the domain, so changing it - and its priority values - is how email flow is redirected to a new provider or filtering service. C (SPF) is published as a TXT record and lists who may send as the domain; it authorizes senders but routes nothing. B (TXT) holds arbitrary verification strings, and D (CNAME) aliases one hostname to another and is not consulted for mail delivery.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting a network issue. Users report that the connection keeps dropping and reconnecting every few seconds. The
 technician:
 Verifies the network configuration settings are correct on the workstation
 Tests the network cable from the workstation to the switch and finds no issues
 Uses a known-good workstation on the existing network cable and replicates the reported issue
 Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.A: Add new network hardware to reduce congestion
options.B: Assign a static IP to the impacted workstations.
options.C: Validate the environment for external interference.
options.D: Check the network logs for evidence of port flapping.

explanation: A known-good workstation on the same cable reproduces the drop, which clears both the PC and the cable and leaves the switch port as the suspect - the switch logs will show the interface cycling up and down, which is port flapping. C (External interference) is a wireless step, and this cabled link already tested good. B (Assign a static IP) does not stop a link dropping, and A (Add new network hardware) treats congestion, which causes slowness rather than disconnects.

question: Which of the following would prevent a virtual machine from communicating with any endpoints on a network or the internet?
explanation: A sandbox is deliberately walled off, with no virtual network adapter bridged to the LAN, so code inside it cannot reach other hosts or the internet - that isolation is the whole point when detonating unknown software. D (Type 1 hypervisor) hosts VMs that are normally attached to virtual switches with full connectivity. A (VDI) requires network access by definition, since the desktop is streamed to a client, and B (Private cloud) is still a routed, connected environment.

question:
A technician recently updated the firmware on a dual-BIOS motherboard. Following the update, the system has been stuck in a boot loop and
 cannot start an OS from any internal or external device. The technician cannot access the UEFI menu either. Which of the following should the
 technician do next?

options.C: Start a warranty repair of the motherboard.
options.D: Reapply thermal paste to the CPU.

explanation: Dual-BIOS boards carry a second, factory or backup firmware image exactly for this scenario; switching to the secondary configuration, usually with a jumper or a dedicated switch, boots from the known-good ROM and restores access to the UEFI menu. B (Downgrade the firmware via USB) is not possible because the system cannot boot or reach the flash utility. C (Warranty repair) skips the built-in recovery feature, and D (Reapply thermal paste) addresses overheating, which does not fit a boot loop that started immediately after a flash.

question: Which of the following cloud models exclusively utilizes a local data center?
explanation: A private cloud is built and operated for one organization on its own hardware in its own data center, giving complete control over where the data physically sits. B (Public) runs entirely on a third-party provider's shared infrastructure. C (Hybrid) deliberately combines local and provider-hosted resources, so it is not exclusive to a local site, and D (Community) is shared infrastructure serving several organizations with common requirements.

question:
A customer has several bare-metal servers running a mix of Windows, Linux, and Unix OSs. The customer wants to consolidate the servers but is
 concerned about data privacy and recurring costs. Which of the following solutions should a technician recommend?
explanation: Containers pack applications into isolated user spaces on shared hosts, consolidating the existing servers with far less overhead than full VMs, keeping everything in-house where the customer controls the data, with no monthly provider bill or per-VM OS licence. A (IaaS) moves workloads to a provider, hitting both the privacy and recurring cost concerns. D (VDI) delivers user desktops rather than consolidating servers, and C (Type 2 hypervisor) stacks guests on a full host OS, the least efficient option. (Note: the dump prints C as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says B — we go with the community.)

question:
A technician is troubleshooting internet connectivity issues after a firewall update. Users report that they can access local network resources,
 such as printers and shares, but cannot access the internet. Which of the following settings is most likely causing the issue?
explanation: Local shares and printers are on the same subnet and need no routing, so the fact that only internet access broke points at the default gateway - if the firewall update changed or removed the gateway address handed out to clients, traffic destined off the subnet has nowhere to go. C (Subnet mask) errors normally break communication with local hosts as well. A (Static IP assignments) alone would not selectively kill outbound traffic, and D (VLANs) misconfiguration would disrupt access to those local resources too.

question:
A help desk technician inspects a laptop keyboard because a single key has stopped working. The technician checks the keyboard for debris.
 Which of the following actions should the technician do next to troubleshoot the issue cost-effectively?
explanation: Debris has already been ruled out, so the cheapest next move is to pop off and reseat or swap the keycap - a cracked, warped or badly seated cap stops the plunger reaching the switch, and caps cost almost nothing. A (Replace the keyboard) is a whole-assembly swap that on many laptops means the entire palmrest, which is exactly the expense the question is avoiding. C (Replace the circuit board) is drastic for one key, and B (Replace the key switch) comes later, after the cap itself is eliminated. (Note: the dump prints B as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says D — we go with the community.)

question:
An end user's domain password expires while they are working from home. The end user tries to reset the password using Ctrl+Alt+Delete and
 then receives the following message:
 Configuration information could not be read from the domain controller, either because the machine is unavailable or because access denied.
 Which of the following will resolve this issue?

options.C: Reset the account in Active Directory.

explanation: Changing a domain password requires the workstation to reach a domain controller, and from home there is no route to it - the error says exactly that. The VPN puts the machine back on the corporate network so the change can process. D (Join the Wi-Fi network) does not help, since the user plainly already has internet. A (Restart the computer) creates no path to the DC, and C (Reset the account in Active Directory) needs an admin and still leaves the user off the domain.

question:
A computer displays an error message indicating there is insufficient storage when installing applications. The user reports slow application load
 times. Which of the following replacement components would best resolve this issue?
explanation: Replacing the drive with a larger SSD solves both complaints at once: more capacity for installing applications and dramatically faster random reads, so programs load quickly. C (HDD) could add capacity but keeps the mechanical latency that makes loading slow. D (RAM) does not create disk space and will not clear an insufficient storage error, and B (USB) flash storage is slow, external and not a suitable place for installed applications.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting a connectivity issue on a network computer. The technician runs ipconfig in a command prompt and receives the
 following IP address: 169.254.0.6. Which of the following is most likely the type of IP address being assigned?
explanation: 169.254.x.x is the APIPA range, which Windows assigns to itself when it broadcasts for DHCP and gets no answer - the address is self-assigned locally rather than issued by any server. B (Dynamic assignment) would come from a DHCP server and fall inside the configured scope, and A (DHCP reservation) is also server-issued, just tied to a MAC address. D (Static assignment) is typed in manually by a technician and would not land in the APIPA range.

question:
Which of the following storage options would a technician most likely recommend to have large amounts of affordable capacity without concern
 for read times on a desktop computer?
explanation: A 2TB 5,400rpm SATA drive gives the most capacity per dollar, and the low spindle speed is irrelevant because read times explicitly do not matter here. A (750GB NVMe M.2 SSD) is fast but smaller and far more expensive per gigabyte. B (2x1TB PCIe SSD in RAID 1) mirrors down to only 1TB of usable space at flash prices, and D (4TB SAS 2.5 15,000rpm HDD) is enterprise hardware priced for performance the user does not need.

question: Which of the following utilizes specialized ports on a laptop to expand the local connection options?
explanation: A docking station connects through the laptop's dedicated docking or proprietary connector and expands it into a desktop setup - multiple displays, wired Ethernet, USB peripherals, sometimes extra drive bays, plus power in the same connection. C (Port replicator) is the closest distractor but simply mirrors the ports the laptop already has, usually over a generic USB link, without adding capability. D (USB dongle) adds one function through a standard port, and A (NFC adapter) is a short-range wireless reader.

question: Which of the following tools would a technician use to connect wires to an RJ45 connector?
explanation: A crimper seats the individual conductors into the RJ45 plug's contact blades and squeezes the strain relief onto the jacket in one action, which is how a patch cable end is made. B (Cable stripper) only removes the outer jacket to expose the pairs before crimping. C (Punchdown) tool is for terminating wires into 110 blocks, patch panels and keystone jacks, and D (Loopback plug) is a test device for checking a port, not a termination tool.

question:
A technician is working on a RAID 1 array that is apparently degraded. The technician verifies the RAM and power are both operating as expected.
 Which of the following can the technician do to further isolate the issue?
explanation: RAM and power are already cleared, so the next step is SMART or vendor diagnostics against each disk individually - that identifies which mirror member is failing before anything is replaced. B (chkdsk /f) checks file system structures, not drive health. C (Rebuild the RAID array) is the fix that follows diagnosis and doing it blind risks rebuilding onto the bad disk, while D (Reconfigure as RAID 0) wipes the data and removes redundancy.

question:
A company wants its RAID array set up so that it could lose multiple drives and still have redundancy. Which of the following configurations should
 the company choose?
explanation: RAID 6 stripes with double distributed parity, so it is the only option here that survives two drives failing at the same time and still serves data, at the cost of two drives' worth of capacity and a minimum of four disks. C (RAID 5) carries single parity and dies on a second failure, which commonly happens during a long rebuild. B (RAID 1) mirrors a pair and tolerates one loss, and A (RAID 0) stripes with no parity, so a single failure takes the whole set.

question:
A user prints a spreadsheet in duplex mode. The spreadsheet is difficult to read because some of the columns spill onto the second side of the
 page. Which of the following should the user do to prevent the issue but still print on both sides of the page?

options.B: Try a smaller font size in the spreadsheet.

explanation: Rotating the sheet to landscape widens the printable area so the extra columns fit on one side, and duplex printing stays enabled as required. A (Turn off duplex printing) directly contradicts the requirement to keep printing on both sides. B (Try a smaller font size) shrinks the text and makes the sheet harder to read, which is the complaint being solved, and D (Use a different print driver) does not change how the spreadsheet is laid out on the page.

question: Which of the following cable types can be used to transfer data and video?
explanation: USB-C carries data, power and video over a single connector, using DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt to drive a display while USB data and charging continue on the same cable. B (HDMI) and C (DisplayPort) transport video and audio only - they were never designed as general purpose data buses. D (VGA) is older still: analog video with no audio and no data capability at all.

question: Which of the following types of RAM is best suited to handle errors within the module itself?
explanation: C (ECC) memory carries an extra chip and check bits so the module can detect multi-bit errors and silently correct single-bit ones as data is read, which is exactly error handling inside the module. A (DIMM) and D (SODIMM) are only physical form factors, desktop and laptop respectively, and say nothing about reliability. B (Dual channel) is a bandwidth arrangement across two modules, not an error-correction feature.

question: A technician needs to move a workstation to a different logical network segment. Which of the following technologies should the technician use?
explanation: B (VLAN) lets an administrator reassign the switch port the workstation plugs into, dropping it into a different broadcast domain and logical subnet without touching a single cable. A (DHCP) only hands out addresses inside whatever segment the port already belongs to, and C (DNS) resolves names to addresses. D (VPN) tunnels traffic securely across an untrusted network for remote access rather than re-segmenting a LAN internally.

question:
After a technician installs a new motherboard, the computer will not start and fails POST. The technician verifies the power supply is functioning
 as expected, and the CPU is installed correctly. Which of the following steps should the technician complete next?
explanation: C (Reseat the RAM) is the next logical check because unseated or improperly seated DIMMs are the most common no-POST cause after a board swap, and memory is easily disturbed during installation. A (Flash the BIOS) is not possible on a machine that will not POST in the first place. B (CMOS battery) produces lost settings and clock drift, not a failed POST, and D (Reinstall the old motherboard) gives up before the free, obvious checks are done.

question: Which of the following is an advantage of using VDI?

options.A: Authentication is not required on a domain.
options.C: Less manual configuration is needed for each workstation.
options.D: A virus is automatically contained locally.

explanation: C (Less manual configuration is needed for each workstation) is the real VDI win: desktops are built from a central golden image on the server, so patching and configuration happen once instead of per endpoint. B (Licensing costs are minimized) is usually the opposite, since VDI adds hypervisor, broker and per-user OS licensing. A is false because domain authentication is still required, and D is wrong because malware in a VDI session lives on the host infrastructure, not safely on the local thin client.

question:
A user is unable to access secure applications on their tablet when working from home a couple days per week, but the applications work when in
 the office. Which of the following services most likely needs to be reconfigured to allow for remote work?
explanation: B (Mobile device management) enforces the policies that decide which apps and corporate resources a tablet may reach and under what conditions, so a policy tied to the office network or a compliance check is what blocks the secure apps from home. C (Wi-Fi Protected Access) is just the wireless encryption standard on the local access point and would break all connectivity, not selected apps. A (GPS) and D (NFC) are location and short-range contactless services with no bearing on application access.

question:
A systems administrator deploys BitLocker to all devices. However, one of the desktop PCs is not able to encrypt the boot drive. Which of the
 following should the administrator check?
explanation: A (TPM) is the chip that seals BitLocker's volume master key to the platform and releases it only after a valid boot measurement, so a PC with the TPM missing or disabled in UEFI cannot encrypt the boot drive by default. B (CPU), C (RAM) and D (HDD) are not what gates BitLocker here; any working drive can be encrypted, and processor and memory play no role in key storage.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting issues occurring on a user's mobile device. Applications and the OS have slow response times, even when
 performing simple tasks, such as writing an email. Additionally, new applications occasionally fail to launch. Which of the following should the
 technician do next?

options.A: Move the device to a room with a colder temperature.
options.D: Check the battery health of the device.

explanation: B (Close unnecessary programs) is the correct next step because background apps consuming RAM and CPU are the usual cause of sluggish response and apps that fail to launch, and it costs nothing and risks no data. C (Reset to factory default settings) is a last resort that wipes the device. D (Check the battery health) matters for shutdowns and throttling but comes later, and A (colder room) only applies if the device is visibly overheating. (Note: the dump prints D as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says B — we go with the community.)

question:
A user connects their laptop to a projector in a conference room. Once connected, the user reports the screen is smaller at the bottom than at the
 top. The user tries restarting the laptop and then disconnecting and reconnecting the cable to the projector. Which of the following should a
 technician do to resolve the issue?
explanation: C (Adjust the keystone) fixes the trapezoid distortion described, where the image is wider at one edge because the projector is not perpendicular to the screen; keystone correction digitally squares the picture back up. D (Increase the resolution) changes pixel count and sharpness, not geometry. A (Replace the HDMI cable) and B (Power cycle the projector) address signal dropouts or lockups, and the user already reseated the cable and rebooted with no change.

question:
A projector has been shutting down after 30 minutes of use, and it has a strange smell. The technician confirms the power source is not the cause
 of the issue. Which of the following steps should the technician take next to resolve this issue?
explanation: C (Clean the filter) targets the actual fault: a clogged intake filter starves the projector of airflow, so it overheats, gives off a hot burning odour, and trips thermal shutdown after roughly half an hour of running. A (Replace the bulb) would show as a dim, discoloured or dead image rather than heat-triggered shutdowns. B (projector configuration) and D (gamma settings) are software and image-quality settings that cannot cause overheating.

question:
A user reports that the printouts from a laser printer have lines and smudges on them. The printer is also intermittently misfeeding the paper.
 Which of the following components should a technician replace to address this issue?
explanation: B (Maintenance kit) is the single replacement that covers both symptoms, since the kit bundles the fuser, transfer roller and pickup/feed rollers that a high-volume laser wears out together, producing streaks and smudges plus misfeeds. A (Fuser) alone explains smudging but not paper pickup problems, and C (Corona wire) affects charge and image quality only. D (Toner cartridge) would cause faded or streaky print but has nothing to do with feeding paper.

question:
A company has a main office and 20 branch offices. The company wants to have a backup network connection to allow connectivity if the main
 fiber connection goes down. The company does not want to create new infrastructure. Which of the following should the company use?
explanation: B (Cellular) needs no new physical plant at all: a cellular modem or router at each site connects over the carrier's existing towers, which suits 20 branches that must not build infrastructure. A (Cable) and C (DSL) both require a provider circuit to be run and provisioned to every location, which is exactly the new infrastructure the company rejected. D (SAN) is a storage area network for block storage, not an internet or WAN failover link.

question: Which of the following drive interfaces is typically used in server systems but not in home computers?
explanation: B (SAS) is the enterprise interface built for servers, offering higher signal rates, full-duplex operation, dual-port paths for redundancy, longer cable runs and support for expanders that address many drives. C (SATA) is the consumer standard found in nearly every home PC. A (NVMe) and D (PCIe) are used in both consumer and server systems, with NVMe drives sitting on the PCIe bus in ordinary desktops and laptops.

question: Which of the following could a user employ to maximize module bandwidth when selecting memory for a high-end gaming computer?
explanation: C (Channel configuration) is what multiplies bandwidth: populating matched modules so the controller runs dual, triple or quad channel gives parallel paths to memory and doubles or better the effective throughput. A (Error correction) adds reliability and if anything a slight latency penalty. B (RAM voltage) is a stability and overclocking headroom setting, and D (Physical module size) refers to capacity or form factor, neither of which widens the memory bus.

question:
An IT specialist compares Bluetooth and NFC technologies for mobile device connectivity. Which of the following statements accurately describes
 a key difference between the two?

options.A: NFC is faster than Bluetooth when transferring large files between devices.
options.B: NFC consumes more power than Bluetooth, making it less suitable for devices in which battery conservation is crucial.
options.C: NFC requires pairing with the receiving host, whereas Bluetooth just needs the available connection.
options.D: NFC works best within a few centimeters, but Bluetooth can connect devices that are up to 32ft (10m) apart.

explanation: D is the accurate contrast: NFC is deliberately limited to about 4cm so a tap is an intentional act, while Bluetooth Class 2 devices typically reach around 10m (33ft). A is backwards because NFC tops out around 424Kbps and is far slower than Bluetooth for file transfer. B is also backwards, as NFC uses very little power and can even run passively. C reverses the pairing requirement, since Bluetooth is the technology that needs a pairing process.

question:
A help desk technician needs to work on a high-volume printer. Users have reported occasional paper jams and smudges appearing on printed
 documents. Which of the following steps should the technician do next to address these issues?

options.C: Change all the ink or toner cartridges.

explanation: B (Check and clean the rollers) addresses both complaints at once: worn or paper-dust-coated pickup and feed rollers slip and jam, and contaminated rollers also transfer marks onto the page. It is also the cheapest, least invasive step. C (Change all the ink or toner cartridges) is wasteful and does not fix jams, D (Replace the fuser) is a costly part swap before diagnosis, and A (factory reset) clears configuration but not a mechanical fault.

question:
A user reports that a phone’s integration features consistently stop and restart when charging the phone in a car. A technician checks the phone
 and finds no malicious applications. Which of the following should the technician do to fix the issue?

options.B: Replace the cable with a longer cable.
options.C: Reinstall MDM software on the phone.

explanation: A (Clean the connection port) is right because lint and debris packed into the charging port stop the connector seating fully, so the data pins make and break contact as the car moves and the integration session keeps dropping and reconnecting. B (a longer cable) does nothing for an intermittent contact. C (Reinstall MDM) is pointless when no malicious app or policy issue was found, and D (Discharge the battery) has no relationship to a physical connection fault.

question:
A technician sets up a conference room projector that begins to intermittently flicker. The projector is connected to a laptop via an HDMI cable.
 When the technician connects the laptop to a monitor using the same cable, the issue persists. Which of the following steps should the technician
 take to troubleshoot the display issue?

options.A: Adjust the resolution settings on the laptop.
options.B: Swap the HDMI cable with a new one.
options.D: Check and configure the refresh rate settings.

explanation: B (Swap the HDMI cable with a new one) follows the isolation the technician already performed: the same cable produced flicker on two different displays, so the shared component is the cable itself. C (Replace the projector) is disproved by the monitor showing the same symptom. A (resolution) and D (refresh rate) would cause no signal, out-of-range messages or tearing on a consistent basis rather than intermittent flicker that follows the cable between devices. (Note: the dump prints D as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says B — we go with the community.)

question:
A SOHO customer runs an OS on a bare-metal server that has been EOL for almost a decade and is showing signs of failure. The application
 meets all the customer’s needs, and they want to continue using it. However, the developer went out of business, and there is no way to upgrade it.
 A technician does not think the OS will run on modern hardware. Which of the following will allow the customer to use the application long-term?

options.A: Continue to use the current system until failure.
options.B: Virtualize the entire system under a compatible hypervisor.
options.C: Containerize the application in a multitenant cloud environment.
options.D: Clone the disks and run the application from a USB enclosure.

explanation: B (Virtualize the entire system under a compatible hypervisor) preserves the legacy OS and application exactly as they are while the hypervisor presents virtualised hardware, so the software runs on modern, supportable servers. A (Continue until failure) ignores the failing hardware and guarantees data loss. C (Containerize) requires the app to be rebuilt for a container runtime, which is impossible with the developer gone and no source. D (USB enclosure) still needs the old OS to boot on incompatible modern hardware.

question: Which of the following network services is used to assign an IP address to a network host?
explanation: A (DHCP) leases IP addresses along with subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server details to hosts as they join the network, which is precisely address assignment. B (DNS) translates hostnames into addresses that already exist. C (LDAP) queries directory services for user and object information, and D (SMTP) transports email between mail servers. None of the last three hand out addressing.

question: Which of the following ports is commonly used for remote desktop connections?
explanation: C (3389) is the TCP and UDP port for RDP, Microsoft's Remote Desktop Protocol. A (137) is NetBIOS name service and B (445) is SMB for Windows file and printer sharing, both legacy or file-sharing ports rather than remote control. D (4443) is a non-standard alternate HTTPS port used by some management appliances but is not associated with remote desktop sessions.

question: Images and text from a laser printer smudge if touched. Which of the following should a technician do to resolve the issue?
explanation: C (Replace the fuser) is correct because the fuser applies the heat and pressure that bonds toner permanently to the paper; if it is failing, toner sits loose on the sheet and rubs off when touched. A (Check the toner levels) explains faded or streaky output, not unfused toner. D (Clean the pickup rollers) fixes feeding and jamming, and B (Install a maintenance kit) is the broader, more expensive option when the specific failed component has already been identified.

question:
A user reports their company-provided smartphone does not have internet access when the user is in the parking lot. Which of the following
 should a technician check first?
explanation: A (3G/4G/5G/LTE settings) should be checked first because the parking lot is outside Wi-Fi range, so the phone must fall back to cellular data; if mobile data or data roaming is toggled off, or the APN is wrong, the device has coverage but no internet. B (SIM connection) would normally kill calls and texts as well and show no service. C (Hotspot capability) shares an existing connection rather than creating one, and D (GPS) only supplies location.

question:
Every day for a week, when a user turns on their computer, the time is wrong. A technician corrects the time, but the issue happens again. Which
 of the following is most likely the cause of the issue?
explanation: D (A faulty CMOS battery) fits perfectly: the coin cell keeps the real-time clock and BIOS settings alive while the machine is off, so when it dies the clock resets or drifts every single power-on and a manual correction never sticks. B (NTP settings) would typically affect every domain machine, not one, and would usually resync rather than lose time at boot. C (Incorrect time zone) produces a constant fixed offset, and A (failing NIC) causes connectivity problems, not timekeeping.

question:
A company decides to subscribe to a cloud service to provide email for its employees. Which of the following cloud models is the company
 adopting?
explanation: B (SaaS) is the model where the provider owns and runs the whole stack and the customer simply consumes the finished application through a browser or client, which is what subscribing to hosted email is. A (PaaS) supplies runtimes and development tooling for the customer to deploy their own code. D (IaaS) rents raw virtual machines, storage and networking that the customer must build the mail server on. C (DaaS) delivers hosted virtual desktops.

question:
A customer reports that a workstation has no internet connectivity. A technician confirms the port is disabled. Which of the following is most
 likely responsible for the issue?
explanation: C (Managed switch) is the only device listed that can administratively disable an individual port, since managed switches expose per-port configuration through a CLI or web interface where a port can be shut down manually or by port security. A (Patch panel) is a passive punch-down block with no logic or configuration. B (Physical NIC) would fail on the workstation side rather than reporting a disabled switch port, and D (firewall) filters traffic between networks rather than switching access ports.

question:
A company is testing the latest model of a laptop. After turning on the laptop, there is a noticeable burning smell. Which of the following steps
 should a technician take to troubleshoot the laptop issue? (Choose two.)

options.A: Turn it off and disconnect all power sources
options.B: Submit an emergency request to the local facilities manager
options.C: Check for foreign objects, liquid spills, and internal damage.
options.D: Contact the vendor and submit a return request.
options.E: Remove the device from the MDM

explanation: A (Turn it off and disconnect all power sources) comes first because a burning smell means something is shorting or overheating and cutting mains and battery power prevents fire or further damage. C (Check for foreign objects, liquid spills, and internal damage) is the diagnostic step that identifies the cause once the unit is safely de-energised. F (alternate AC adapter) reapplies power to a suspect device, D (return request) skips diagnosis, B (facilities manager) applies to a building emergency, and E (MDM removal) is unrelated to hardware safety.

question:
A technician needs to figure out why a laser printer is intermittently not feeding paper to print. The technician verifies the issue by running several
 copy-and-print tests. Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: C (Clean the pickup rollers) is the next step because the rubber rollers that grab sheets from the tray glaze over with paper dust and lose grip, which is exactly what causes intermittent failure to feed. A (Update the printer drivers) affects how jobs are rendered, not paper handling. B (Select the correct paper size) would produce consistent errors or wrong-tray prompts rather than random misfeeds, and D (Replace the toner cartridge) only influences image quality.

question: Which of the following can be used to logically segment networks?
explanation: B (VLAN) creates separate broadcast domains on shared physical switching hardware, so hosts can be grouped logically by function or department regardless of where they plug in. A (MAC) is a hardware address that identifies a NIC and is only a criterion a switch might use, not a segmentation technology by itself. C (NIC) is the adapter in a single host, and D (DSL) is a broadband access technology over telephone lines.

question:
After troubleshooting a computer's connectivity, the network team determines there is a port-flapping issue. After plugging the patch cable into a
 different port, the issue persists. Which of the following troubleshooting steps should a technician take next to resolve the issue?

options.A: Convert the patch cable to a crossover cable
options.B: Test the patch cable from the computer to the network closet
options.C: Verify the length of the patch cable meets current standards
options.D: Replace the patch cable from the device to the wall

explanation: D (Replace the patch cable from the device to the wall) is the next move because moving to a different switch port ruled out the port, leaving the user-side patch cable as the likeliest cause of the link flapping up and down. B refers to the permanent structured cabling between the wall jack and the closet, not the patch cable. A (crossover cable) is unnecessary with modern auto-MDIX gear, and C (length) is a fixed design factor that would not suddenly begin flapping. (Note: the dump prints B as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says D — we go with the community.)

question:
A user is testing a new OS that is contained on a USB drive. The user wants the new OS to load automatically when the computer is turned on.
 Which of the following should the user configure?
explanation: D (Boot options) is where the boot order or boot priority in BIOS/UEFI is set, so putting USB ahead of the internal drive makes the machine load the removable OS automatically at power-on. A (BIOS password) only restricts access to firmware setup. B (Trusted Platform Module) stores keys for encryption such as BitLocker and Secure Boot measurements, and C (USB permissions) governs OS-level access to removable media after boot, not what the firmware boots from.

question:
A technician is setting up a locally hosted environment for internal developers who need concurrent access to a wide array of test OSs. Which of
 the following would best fulfill this requirement?
explanation: A (Hypervisor) is what allows many guest operating systems to run side by side on one host at the same time, giving developers simultaneous access to a range of test OSs locally. C (Multiboot server computer) can hold several OSs but only one can be running at any moment, which defeats concurrent access. B (SaaS platform) delivers finished applications rather than operating systems and is not locally hosted, and D (Sandbox) isolates a single process or environment for safe execution.

question:
An employee’s screen keeps flashing. Sometimes the picture goes out and comes back. The employee checks the power cord and confirms the
 device is plugged in fully. Which of the following should a technician check for first?
explanation: A (Loose video cable) is the first thing to check because a partially seated or damaged display cable makes the picture flicker and drop out intermittently, and it costs nothing to reseat. B (Failing graphics card) and D (Swollen motherboard capacitor) are real but far less common hardware failures that are checked after the simple physical connections. C (Conflicting drivers) typically shows as artefacts, resolution problems or crashes after an update rather than a picture that comes and goes.

question:
A technician is setting up a scan-to-SMB function on a multifunction printer. Which of the following connection types should the technician
 configure?
explanation: C (Network share) is what scan-to-SMB targets: SMB is the Windows file-sharing protocol, so the MFP is pointed at a shared folder path with credentials and drops the scanned file there. A (Email server) is used for scan-to-email over SMTP instead. B (SFTP connection) is a different protocol on port 22 requiring an SSH file server, and D (Print services) handles inbound print jobs, which is the opposite direction from scanning.

question:
A user reports that the print quality of their desk printer is poor. A technician replaces the ink cartridge, but this does not resolve the issue. Which
 of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: B (Clean the printheads) is the next step for an inkjet whose output is still poor after a new cartridge, because dried ink clogs the nozzles and produces banding, missing colours and streaks; the printer's built-in head cleaning utility clears them. A (Replace the pickup rollers) fixes feeding and jams, not quality. C (Switch the paper type) causes bleeding or dullness only in specific media mismatches, and D (Change the ribbon) applies to impact and dye-sublimation printers, not inkjets.

question:
An end user reports that their laptop shuts down when they undock it. Even when using a new charging cable, the issue persists. Which of the
 following should the technician do next?
explanation: D (Replace the battery) follows directly from the symptom: the laptop runs fine on dock power but dies the instant it must draw from the battery, which means the battery no longer holds a usable charge. C (Try a different charger) has effectively been done, since a new charging cable made no difference and the machine works while powered. A (Flash the BIOS) and B (Update the drivers) are software steps that do not explain an immediate power loss when external power is removed.

question:
A company provides cell phones to employees who travel internationally. An employee brings their phone to the help desk so the necessary
 equipment can be installed. However, the technician cannot install any new hardware on the phone. Which of the following will the technician
 require so the phone can connect to a different provider?
explanation: C (eSIM) solves it because the embedded SIM is already soldered into the phone and is provisioned entirely in software, so an international carrier profile can be downloaded without installing any hardware. A (USB-C) is a charging and data connector, and B (SD card) adds storage rather than carrier identity. D (MDM) manages policies and applications on the device but cannot register the phone with a different mobile network operator.

question:
Which of the following internet connection types provides the fastest speeds and greatest coverage in less populated areas with minimal
 infrastructure?
explanation: D (Cellular) wins on coverage where infrastructure is thin, since a tower serves a wide rural footprint and each subscriber needs only a modem or hotspot rather than a cable run to the premises, and modern LTE and 5G deliver strong speeds. A (Fiber) is the fastest technology overall but requires expensive trenching that rarely reaches sparsely populated areas. B (Cable) depends on existing coaxial plant, and C (DSL) degrades badly with distance from the central office.

question: Which of the following ports should a technician disable to increase the security of remote connectivity?
explanation: B (23) is Telnet, which carries credentials and session data in clear text, so disabling it and using SSH instead is the standard hardening step for remote connectivity. A (22) is SSH itself, the encrypted replacement you want to keep. C (25) is SMTP for mail transfer and D (53) is DNS name resolution; both are unrelated to remote administration and disabling them would break mail and lookups.

question:
A network operations analyst receives an automated alert regarding a server with an array. The analyst walks over to the server and sees a
 blinking orange light at the hard disk bay. The server is configured for RAID 1. Which of the following should the analyst do to resolve this issue?

options.B: Undo the array and create a new one
options.D: Replace the hard disk and rebuild the array

explanation: D (Replace the hard disk and rebuild the array) is correct because an amber or blinking orange bay light signals a failed or predicted-failure drive, and RAID 1 is now running degraded on its surviving mirror with no redundancy left. A (Change the array to RAID 0) removes redundancy entirely and destroys data. B (Undo the array and create a new one) needlessly wipes a recoverable array, and C (Update RAID card firmware) does not address a physically failed disk.

question:
A user returns from a trip and discovers a computer that is connected to the LAN times out intermittently. Upon investigation, a technician finds
 the RJ45 pin is not properly terminated. Which of the following networking tools is most appropriate to fix the issue?
explanation: D (Crimper) is the tool that cuts off the bad plug, seats the conductors in a fresh RJ45 and presses the contacts into the copper to make a proper termination. B (Cable tester) only confirms which pins fail; it does not fix anything. A (Toner probe) traces and locates cable runs, and C (Punchdown) is used to seat wires into 110 blocks on patch panels and keystone jacks, not onto an RJ45 plug.

question:
A technician upgrades a PC with two DIMMs, for a total of 32GB. After installing the two DIMMs, the user notices the OS is reporting only 16GB.
 Which of the following tasks should the technician perform to resolve the issue in the most rapid, cost-effective way possible?

options.C: Update the OS to the latest version

explanation: B (Reinstall RAM in different slots) is the fastest free fix, since a module that is not fully seated or is sitting in the wrong slot for the board's channel layout often leaves half the memory unrecognised, and moving the sticks also isolates a bad slot. A (Roll back updates) and C (Update the OS) chase a software cause when the symptom appeared immediately after a hardware change. D (Replace the motherboard) is the expensive last resort, not the first move.

question: Which of the following internet connection types is the best for extremely high data transfer with symmetrical upload and download speeds?
explanation: C (Fiber) transmits light over glass with enormous bandwidth and is provisioned symmetrically, so upload matches download, which is what the requirement calls for. A (DSL) is asymmetric by design and limited by copper distance. B (Cellular) varies with signal and tower congestion and is normally asymmetric, and D (Satellite) suffers high latency and much slower uplink than downlink.

question:
A company wants to have fast read speeds for its locally stored data. Which of the following configurations has the lowest cost to fulfill this
 requirement?
explanation: A (RAID 0) stripes data across drives so reads come from multiple disks in parallel, and it uses 100 percent of the raw capacity, making it the cheapest way to get speed. B (RAID 1) mirrors and wastes half the capacity, and D (RAID 10) needs at least four drives and gives up half of them to mirroring. C (RAID 5) sacrifices one drive's worth of space to parity and adds write overhead, so all three cost more per usable gigabyte.

question: Which of the following connectors can be used to charge most modern mobile devices and may have the capacity to send data audio, and video?
explanation: B (USB-C) is the reversible modern standard that carries power delivery for charging, data, and video via DisplayPort or Thunderbolt alternate mode, matching every part of the description. A (Lightning) is Apple-proprietary and being phased out, so it is not on most devices. C (MicroUSB) and D (MiniUSB) are older, slower connectors with limited charging capability and no native video support.

question: Which of the following devices has ACL capabilities?
explanation: C (Firewall) is built around access control lists, evaluating traffic against ordered permit and deny rules based on source and destination IP, port and protocol. D (Unmanaged switch) has no configuration interface at all, so it cannot hold rules. A (PoE injector) simply adds DC power onto an Ethernet run, and B (DSL) is a broadband access technology; neither inspects or filters traffic.

question:
A user would like to connect a laptop to a monitor, keyboard, and mouse when in the office. The user prefers to use as few cables as possible.
 Which of the following would best achieve that goal?
explanation: C (Docking station) is the answer because a single connection to the dock carries the monitor's video plus the USB keyboard and mouse, so the laptop needs one cable when the user sits down. A (Bluetooth) can handle the keyboard and mouse but cannot drive an external monitor, so a video cable is still required. B (Managed switch) provides network ports only, and D (NFC) is a centimetre-range contactless technology for tap transactions, not peripherals.

question:
A user keeps getting an error message when trying to print a letter. The printer is normally used to print cards and invitations. The user tries
 printing from a different computer, but the issue persists. Which of the following should the user do to resolve the issue?
explanation: D (Change the paper tray setting) is right because the tray is configured for the card stock the printer normally uses, so a letter-sized job finds no matching tray and errors out; correcting the tray's paper size and type clears it. B (Print on card stock) works around the problem instead of resolving it. C (Replace the rollers) targets jams and misfeeds, and A (Print fewer pages) is irrelevant since the fault followed the document to a second computer.

question: Which of the following should a company use to implement automatic time synchronization?
explanation: C (NTP) is the Network Time Protocol, which keeps clients synchronised to an authoritative time source automatically and is essential for logging, certificates and Kerberos authentication. A (DHCP) assigns addressing and can advertise a time server option but does not perform the synchronisation itself. B (UTM) is an all-in-one security appliance, and D (AAA) covers authentication, authorisation and accounting.

question:
An end user reports that their laptop has a blank screen. A technician observes the keyboard lights are on, and the fan is running. Which of the
 following should the technician do next?
explanation: D (Connect to an external monitor) is the next step because a running fan and lit keyboard prove the system is powered and likely posting, so an external display instantly determines whether the fault is the built-in panel and its cabling or the GPU and motherboard.
