E (Linux) limits game compatibility, and F (TPM 2.0) is a Windows 11 security requirement, not a performance feature.

question:
A technician needs to scan-to-file from a legacy printer. The technician sets up a shared drive but then is unable to view the scanned files. The
 technician confirms their credentials are valid. Which of the following should the technician do to the computer to view the scanned files?

options.A: Disable the firewall on the desktop PC.
options.B: Add a $ to the end of the share name.

explanation: Legacy multifunction devices often speak only the original SMBv1/CIFS dialect, which modern Windows leaves disabled, so the scans never land anywhere the technician can see even though the share and credentials are valid; re-enabling SMB 1.0 in Windows Features restores compatibility. A (disabling the firewall) and D (removing anti-malware) weaken security without touching the dialect mismatch, and B (appending a $) merely hides the share from network browsing.

question: Which of the following is the standard for Wi-Fi 7?
explanation: 802.11be, marketed as Wi-Fi 7, is the standard that adds 320MHz channels, 4096-QAM and Multi-Link Operation on top of Wi-Fi 6E. A (802.1X) is port-based network access control used for enterprise authentication, B (802.3at) is PoE+ supplying up to 30W over Ethernet, and D (802.15.1) is the IEEE specification behind Bluetooth, so none of those are Wi-Fi standards at all.

question:
A user’s phone does not charge consistently, even after a new cable is used to try to charge the phone. The phone's battery is not swollen. Which
 of the following should a technician try next to fix the phone?

options.A: Reset the phone to factory default settings.
options.C: Arrange for repairs at a service center.

explanation: Pocket lint compacted into the charging port stops the connector seating fully, producing exactly this intermittent charging even with a known-good cable, and carefully clearing the port is quick, free and non-destructive. B (Change the battery) is unwarranted when the battery is not swollen and there is no sign it fails to hold a charge, while A (factory reset) and C (service center repairs) are escalations that belong after the simple physical check.

question: Which of the following cloud models exclusively uses dedicated resources?
explanation: A private cloud's compute, storage and network resources are dedicated to one organization, whether hosted on-premises or by a provider, which gives full control and no shared tenancy. D (Public) is multitenant by definition, and A (Community) shares infrastructure among several organizations with a common interest. B (Hybrid) mixes private and public, so part of it is explicitly not dedicated.

question:
An engineer must implement a solution to facilitate and maintain an organization's legacy application until it is retired. The application is currently
 hosted on three physical servers. Which of the following is the most suitable concept for this purpose?
explanation: Virtualizing the three physical servers preserves the legacy application exactly as it runs today while removing the dependency on aging hardware, and the VMs can be snapshotted and consolidated onto much less equipment until retirement day arrives. B (FaaS) would require rewriting the application as functions, A (SAN) only provides shared block storage, and D (configuration management platform) automates server builds but does nothing about the hardware hosting the app.

question: Which of the following is used to reduce cabling requirements to specific security cameras?
explanation: Power over Ethernet carries data and DC power over the single Cat 5e/6 run to each camera, so no separate electrical circuit or outlet has to be installed at the mounting point. C (ONT) terminates a fiber service at the building, B (DSL) is broadband over telephone lines, and D (NIC) is the network adapter inside a host, so none of them removes a cable from the camera installation.

question:
A user’s computer system does not complete the startup process and shows the following message:
 No boot disk found.
 The system does pass the HDD diagnostic test. Which of the following should the technician do to resolve the issue?

options.A: Change the BIOS from legacy to UEFI.
options.B: Replace the HDD with an NVMe drive.
options.D: Upgrade the operating system to Windows 11.

explanation: The disk itself is healthy, so the firmware is simply not looking for the bootloader the right way: an OS installed on a GPT disk boots only in UEFI mode, and a system left in legacy/CSM mode finds no MBR boot sector and reports no boot disk. B (replacing a working HDD) and D (upgrading the OS) do not address a firmware setting, and C (disabling Secure Boot) relaxes signature checks but still leaves legacy mode unable to boot a GPT installation.

question:
A user has issues selecting objects on their tablet. The user tries to select an object, and the object that opens is to the right of the object that the
 user selects. Which of the following should a technician do to troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: The digitizer maps touch coordinates onto screen coordinates, and when that mapping drifts every tap registers a consistent distance off in one direction, exactly as described; recalibrating realigns the touch layer with the display. A (Change the stylus) is irrelevant when finger input is equally offset, D (clean the screen) addresses dead or erratic patches rather than a uniform shift, and C (malware) does not produce a systematic coordinate offset.

question: Which of the following RAID configurations provides redundancy and better performance without the added work of parity calculations?
explanation: RAID 10 stripes across mirrored pairs, so it gets the read and write speed of striping and survives a drive failure in each mirror, all without calculating parity on every write. B (RAID 5) and C (RAID 6) are redundant but pay a parity write penalty and rebuild slowly. A (RAID 0) stripes for pure performance with no redundancy at all, so a single dead drive loses the entire array.

question: Which of the following is typically found in server memory modules?
explanation: Server DIMMs carry an extra memory chip for error-correcting code, letting the controller detect and repair single-bit errors before they corrupt data or crash a machine expected to run for months. A (RGB) is cosmetic lighting on enthusiast desktop modules. C (Static) refers to SRAM, which is used for CPU cache rather than main memory sticks, and D (SODIMM) is the small form factor used in laptops and mini PCs.

question:
An employee requires a workstation with three high-end graphics cards to render 3-D models. A technician must choose a power supply that
 meets the power requirements for the components and takes into consideration the mission-critical nature of the work. Which of the following
 meet the requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation: High-end graphics cards pull nearly all their power from the 12V rail through the PCIe power connectors, so the supply must deliver enough 12V amperage to feed three of them. Redundancy adds a second power module that takes over if one fails, which is what the mission-critical requirement calls for. B (Modularity) is only cable-management convenience, C (a 20-pin connector) is obsolete since modern boards need 24-pin, and E and F are present on any standard unit.

question:
An IP address is automatically assigned to a single workstation in an office, but the technician confirms the IP address is not in the lease pool.
 This workstation is having issues accessing the internet and internal fileshares. Which of the following address types has been automatically
 assigned?
explanation: An address that appears automatically yet falls outside the DHCP scope is the 169.254.x.x APIPA address Windows self-assigns when no DHCP server responds; it carries no gateway or DNS, which is why both the internet and internal fileshares are unreachable. C (DHCP) would have issued something from the lease pool. B (Static) is typed in by hand rather than assigned automatically, and D (Public IP) would come from the ISP, not appear spontaneously.

question:
All VoIP phone users at a call center report that they get distorted audio and drops in conversations during peak working hours. A technician
 updates the firmware on the phones, but the issue persists. Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.B: Verify that the users’ extensions are in the correct call groups.
options.C: Reset the phones to factory settings and provision them.
options.D: Ask the network team to check the VLAN for QoS.

explanation: Distortion and dropped calls that surface only at peak hours point to congestion, with voice packets arriving late or out of order, so the next step is having the network team confirm the voice VLAN is tagging and prioritizing RTP traffic through QoS. A (replacing every patch cable) would cause errors all day rather than just at busy times. B (call groups) affects call routing, not audio quality, and C (re-provisioning phones) just repeats the firmware step that already failed.

question: Which of the following describes a cloud computing system's ability to use changing levels of resources based on demand?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to scale resources up when demand spikes and release them again when it falls, automatically and on short notice. D (Metered usage) is the billing model that charges for what was consumed, which is a consequence of elasticity rather than the capability itself. B (Multitenancy) means several customers share the same underlying hardware, and A (Availability) describes uptime and resilience.

question: A technician needs to prevent a 3-D-rendering desktop from throttling. Which of the following is the best way to address this issue?

options.A: Enabling the CPU fan through the application
options.B: Switching to a modular power supply

explanation: Thermal throttling happens when the CPU or GPU reaches its temperature limit and clocks itself down, so improving heat removal with a better heat sink, and the airflow to support it, is what keeps the rendering workstation at full speed. B (modular power supply) changes only cabling, D (memory timings) affects RAM latency rather than core temperature, and A is not a real option since fan speed is driven by firmware fan curves, not by the application.

question:
A customer contacts the help desk to report they can access the corporate fileshare but cannot browse the internet. The technician runs ipconfig
 and receives the following output:
 Which of the following is most likely causing the issue?
explanation: Traffic to the fileshare stays on the local subnet and works, while anything bound for the internet must be handed to the default gateway, so a wrong or missing gateway, the next hop, breaks exactly that split. A (corrupt NIC drivers) or D (an unplugged cable) would kill all connectivity including the fileshare. B (a conflicting IPv4 address) usually causes intermittent failures to every destination plus a duplicate-address warning.

question:
A workstation is making clicking sounds inside the case. The UEFI POST takes longer than usual, but the system starts up and all the programs
 function normally. Which of the following should a technician enable in the UEFI to troubleshoot this issue?
explanation: Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology makes the drive report its own reallocated sectors, seek errors and overall health, so enabling it in UEFI lets the technician confirm that the clicking noise and the drawn-out POST come from a failing disk. A (TPM) handles encryption keys and platform integrity, B (Hyperthreading) exposes extra logical cores, and C (virtualization extensions) enable hypervisors, so none of them report drive health.

question:
A user notices a clicking sound each time they turn on a workstation, and it takes a long time for the system to start up. Which of the following
 should the technician replace?
explanation: Clicking is a mechanical sound, the actuator arm repeatedly resetting when it cannot read a sector, which only a spinning platter drive can make, and those retries are what stretch out the startup time. D (SSD) has no moving parts and is silent, C (RAM) fails with beep codes, crashes or a dead POST rather than noise, and A (a failing fan) grinds or whines continuously but would not slow the boot process.

question:
A customer is upgrading an engineering workstation with multiple video cards and storage drives. Which of the following should the customer
 consider first when identifying a new power supply?
explanation: Multiple video cards and extra drives raise the total draw sharply, so the first thing to establish is whether a candidate supply delivers enough total wattage with some headroom, since nothing else matters if the system is starved. B (Connector quantity) does matter but is checked once capacity is settled. A (Input voltage) is dictated by the mains, and C (output voltage) rails are fixed at 3.3V, 5V and 12V on every ATX unit.

question:
A technician is configuring a laptop with an IP address that will not change but will be assigned dynamically. Which of the following configurations
 should the technician use to achieve this goal?
explanation: A DHCP reservation binds a specific IP address to the laptop's MAC address, so the client still leases its configuration dynamically but is always handed the same address. A (Exclusion) pulls addresses out of the pool so DHCP never issues them, C (Scope) defines the range of addresses the server can offer, and B (Lease) is just how long an assignment stays valid, so none of them pin one client to one address.

question: Which of the following resolutions does the Full HD standard use?
explanation: Full HD, also written 1080p, is 1920x1080 pixels. A (1280x720) is HD or 720p, C (3840x2160) is 4K UHD, and D (7680x4320) is 8K UHD. For the HD standards the name comes from the vertical pixel count, while the 4K and 8K labels refer to the approximate horizontal pixel count instead.

question: Which of the following can be used by a mobile device to access a secure building?
explanation: B (Near-field communication) works only over a few centimetres, which is exactly what a door reader needs: the phone is tapped against the panel and passes a stored credential like a proximity badge. A (Hotspot) shares the phone's cellular data with other devices. C (Infrared scanner) is a line-of-sight remote-control technology, not a credential. D (Geolocation) reports where the device is but never authenticates it to a lock.

question: An organization uses a vendor-hosted database server. Which of the following best describes this solution?
explanation: B (PaaS) fits because the vendor owns and maintains the platform - hardware, OS, and the database engine itself, including patching - while the customer only loads schemas and data. C (IaaS) would deliver bare virtual machines and storage that the customer must install and maintain the database on. D (SaaS) is a finished end-user application such as webmail, and A (Hybrid cloud) is a deployment model, not a service model.

question:
A human resources manager printed a sensitive employee termination announcement and forgot to retrieve the document from the printer. Which
 of the following is a way to avoid this situation?
explanation: A (Badging), or secure/pull printing, holds the job on the print server until the owner taps a badge at the device, so a sensitive page never sits unattended in the output tray. B (Duplex) only makes the job two-sided. C (Printer share) simply publishes the printer to the network, which increases exposure rather than reducing it. D (Wireless encryption) protects the job in transit, but the leak here is a physical sheet of paper.

question: Which of the following characteristics differentiates DDR4 RAM from DDR3 RAM?
explanation: A (Lower operating voltage) is the headline change: DDR4 runs at 1.2V against DDR3's 1.5V, cutting power and heat. B (Higher latency) is not a design goal - CAS numbers rise, but the faster clock keeps real-world latency similar. C (Increased DIMM width) is wrong because both remain 64-bit modules; DDR4 adds pins (288 vs 240) and moves the notch, not the data width. D (Single-sided modules) is unrelated to the standard.

question:
A software developer wants to test a new application in an environment that limits access to the OS. Which of the following should the developer
 implement?
explanation: A (Container) packages the app with just its libraries and dependencies, isolating it from the host filesystem and other processes while sharing the kernel - a tightly limited environment ideal for testing. B (Type 2 hypervisor) spins up an entire guest OS, which is heavier and gives the app a full operating system rather than restricted access. C (VDI) delivers virtual desktops to end users, and D (Quarantined PC) is a physical machine used for suspect files, not a development sandbox.

question:
A technician is manually configuring network settings on a user’s computer to route network traffic to a newly deployed firewall. Which of the
 following should the technician change?
explanation: B (Gateway) is the address a host sends traffic to when the destination is outside its own subnet, so pointing the default gateway at the new firewall pushes all outbound traffic through it. C (Subnet mask) only defines how large the local subnet is and which addresses are considered local. D (VLAN) segments traffic at layer 2 on the switch, not in the workstation's IP settings. A (VPN) builds an encrypted tunnel and does not redirect normal LAN routing.

question: Which of the following is used to verify that an emailer is allowed and designated to send emails from a particular IP address?
explanation: B (SPF) is a DNS TXT record that lists the IP addresses and hosts authorized to send mail for a domain; the receiving server compares the connecting IP against that list. C (DKIM) uses a cryptographic signature to prove the message was not altered and came from the domain, which is signature-based rather than IP-based. D (DMARC) only tells receivers what to do when SPF or DKIM fails. A (CNAME) creates a hostname alias.

question: Which of the following describes an environment in which virtual machines are hosted on premises and in a cloud?
explanation: A (Hybrid) by definition mixes private on-premises infrastructure with public cloud resources, with the two connected so workloads and data can move between them. B (Public) would mean everything runs in a shared provider environment, and C (Private) would mean everything stays on the organization's own dedicated infrastructure - neither covers both locations. D (SaaS) is a service model describing hosted applications, not where virtual machines live.

question:
A user is trying to print diagrams on 11in x 17in (28cm x 43cm) paper. The correct paper is in the printer, but the printer prompts the user to insert
 paper. A technician assisting the user successfully prints the diagram to a different printer that is the same model. Which of the following is the
 most likely cause of this issue on the user's printer?
explanation: A (Tray settings) is the cause: the tray is still configured for a smaller size such as Letter, so when the job requests 11x17 the printer sees no matching source and asks for paper. B (Incorrect driver) and C (Connectivity issues) are ruled out because the same file printed fine on an identical model, and connectivity problems would stop the job entirely rather than produce a paper prompt. D (Insufficient permissions) would block printing, not request a different sheet.

question:
A technician installs an external camera on a user's laptop. When loading the company meeting software, the video preview shows a blank screen.
 Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.B: Replace the camera with a different model.
options.C: Update the camera software to the latest version.
options.D: Check the camera's cable for damage or pinches.

explanation: A (Select the correct camera source) is the next step because the meeting software is still bound to the built-in webcam or a disabled default device, which renders a blank preview. It costs nothing to check and matches the troubleshooting rule of testing the simplest cause first. B (Replace the camera) is premature hardware swapping, C (Update the camera software) is a later step if source selection fails, and D (Check the cable) would usually leave the camera undetected rather than showing a blank feed.

question: Which of the following tools will a technician most likely use to identify an unlabeled network connection?
explanation: D (Toner probe) is the tool for this: a tone generator is clipped to one end of the unknown cable and the inductive probe is swept over the punchdown block or patch panel until it squeals on the matching run. C (Cable tester) confirms continuity and wiremap but cannot pick one cable out of a bundle. A (Network tap) copies live traffic for analysis, and B (Loopback plug) only tests whether a port can transmit and receive.

question:
The Chief Information Security Officer asks a technician to inventory desktop PCs to determine which ones meet the requirements for Secure
 Boot. The technician must also configure the PCs for non-user-controllable keys. Which of the following are necessary to meet the enhanced
 security requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation: C (TPM) supplies the hardware-protected key storage that holds the Secure Boot keys where users cannot alter them, and D (UEFI) is the firmware type that actually implements Secure Boot - legacy BIOS has no such feature. B (BIOS password) protects firmware settings but cannot validate boot signatures. A (VDI), E (Disabled boot drive), and F (USB permissions) address desktop delivery or removable media, none of which relate to verifying the boot chain.

question:
A user reports that they cannot get their laptop to work with a video projector connected with an HDMI cable. The projector is turned on, the HDMI
 cable is securely connected on both ends, and the laptop displays properly on its own screen. The display mode is set to "Duplicate" on the laptop.
 Which of the following is most likely causing the issue?

options.A: The projector does not support HDMI connections.
options.B: The laptop display mode should be set to "Extend".
options.C: An HDMI port on the projector failed.
options.D: The input source is incorrect on the projector.

explanation: D (The input source is incorrect on the projector) is the most likely cause: projectors have multiple inputs and must be switched to the HDMI port in use, otherwise they display a blank or no-signal screen even with a good cable. B (Extend) is wrong because Duplicate is the appropriate mode for mirroring a presentation. A (No HDMI support) is contradicted by the cable being connected to an HDMI port, and C (Failed port) is possible but far less common than a wrong input.

question: Which of the following cable types must be used when running copper network cable through a suspended ceiling that is used for air ventilation?
explanation: A (Plenum) cable uses fire-resistant, low-smoke jacketing such as FEP, which is required by code in air-handling spaces like a suspended ceiling used for return air, because standard PVC gives off toxic smoke when it burns. D (Twisted pair) describes the conductor arrangement, not the jacket rating, so it can be either plenum or riser. B (Multimode) is fiber, and C (Coaxial) is a different media type; the question specifically calls for copper network cable.

question:
A computer training institute needs to implement multiple VLANs that must:
 • Connect to each other with minimum hardware.
 • Communicate traffic at wire speed.
 Which of the following is the most suitable?
explanation: C (Layer 3 switch) routes between VLANs in hardware ASICs at wire speed while keeping everything in one device, meeting both the minimum-hardware and full-speed requirements. D (Router) can also route between VLANs, but it means adding a separate device or a router-on-a-stick trunk, where all inter-VLAN traffic squeezes through a single software-forwarded link. A (Web application firewall) inspects HTTP traffic, and B (DDoS appliance) mitigates floods; neither performs inter-VLAN routing.

question:
A small business is growing and wants to scale its computing capacity. The business wants to continue using on-site equipment until it is EOL.
 The solution must be able to share data with the local data center. Which of the following models should a technician suggest?
explanation: C (Hybrid) is the fit because the business keeps its existing on-site hardware until end of life while adding cloud capacity, with connectivity between the two so data is shared with the local data center. A (Public) alone would mean abandoning the on-premises gear now. D (Private) provides dedicated infrastructure but does not add the elastic public capacity being requested, and B (Community) is for multiple organizations with shared compliance needs. E (SaaS) is a service model, not a deployment approach.

question:
A company implements a new policy that prohibits users from installing unapproved applications on corporate tablets. Which of the following
 should the technician use to enforce this policy?
explanation: A (MDM) is the tool that pushes configuration profiles to enrolled tablets, including application allow lists and blocks on sideloading or store installs, and it can report or wipe devices that violate policy. B (ACL) controls access to network resources or files, not what software a device may install. C (DRM) restricts copying of licensed content, and D (PAM) manages privileged administrator accounts and credential vaulting on servers.

question: Which of the following connectors will uplink a new ISP cable modem to its wall jack?
explanation: A (F-type) is the threaded coaxial connector used on RG-6 cable between the wall jack and a cable modem's RF input. C (RJ45) is the eight-pin Ethernet connector used on the modem's LAN side to reach a router or PC, not the incoming ISP side. B (LC) is a small form-factor fiber connector found on optical transceivers, and D (Lightning) is Apple's proprietary mobile device connector.

question: Which of the following types of RAM is most likely used in data centers and in high-performance machines?
explanation: D (RDIMM) is the registered module used in servers and workstations: a register buffers address and command signals between the memory controller and the DRAM chips, letting the system support far more modules and much larger capacity per channel. A (ECC) is error correction, a feature RDIMMs normally include but which is also available on ordinary unbuffered modules. C (Unbuffered) is the standard desktop type with no register, and B (Single-channel) halves or quarters bandwidth.

question: Which of the following wireless frequency ranges involves the use of channels 1, 6, and 11?
explanation: A (2.4GHz) is the band in question - it has 11 usable channels in North America and, at 20MHz spacing, only 1, 6, and 11 avoid overlapping each other. B (5GHz) offers many more non-overlapping channels numbered in the 30s through 160s, and C (6GHz), used by Wi-Fi 6E, adds still more. D (60GHz) is the very short-range WiGig/802.11ad band with its own separate channel plan.

question: Following a power outage, a laptop will not turn on. Which of the following should a technician replace first to resolve the issue?
explanation: A (The AC adapter) is the first thing to swap: a surge or outage most often kills the external power brick, and a laptop with a dead adapter and a drained battery will not power on at all. D (The battery) is less likely because the machine should still run on wall power if the adapter is good. C (The inverter) only drives the backlight on older CCFL panels, so the system would still power up. B (The RAM) usually produces beeps or a blank POST rather than no power.

question: Which of the following should a technician create to assign a permanent IP address to a PC using DHCP?
explanation: A (Reservation) binds a specific MAC address to a specific IP inside the DHCP scope, so the PC always receives the same address while still pulling gateway, DNS, and other options from the server. B (Lease) is just the temporary assignment with an expiry timer. C (Exclusion) removes addresses from the pool so DHCP never hands them out, which supports manual static assignment but does not assign anything. D (Scope option) delivers settings like DNS servers, not the address itself.

question:
A customer is using port 110 for email. However, the customer wants to upgrade to a more secure connection that automatically synchronizes
 with the server. Which of the following should the customer use?
explanation: A (IMAP) is the fix: port 110 is POP3, which typically downloads and removes mail, while IMAP keeps messages on the server and synchronizes folders, read status, and deletions across every client, and it runs encrypted over port 993. C (SMTP) only sends outbound mail, so it cannot replace a retrieval protocol. B (HTTPS) is web traffic and D (SFTP) is secure file transfer; neither is a mailbox access protocol.

question:
Two workstations are connected to a LAN that does not have internet access. A user reports that they are unable to access a network service
 after a power outage. The web page warns the user that the site is insecure. Which of the following will most likely resolve the certificate error?
 (Choose two.)

options.B: Setting the system date and time in the BIOS
options.E: Opening the HTTPS port on the workstation’s firewall
options.F: Scanning the LAN for unauthorized devices

explanation: B (Setting the system date and time in the BIOS) fixes the immediate error, because a clock that reset to a date outside the certificate's validity window makes every certificate look invalid. C (Replacing the CMOS battery) stops it from happening again, since a dead battery is why the clock lost time during the outage. A (Renewing the SSL certificate) targets the server when the fault is clearly the client's clock, and D (Adjusting browser security settings) just hides a real warning.

question:
A small company recently added VoIP through its ISP. Users report intermittent call quality issues during peak hours. Which of the following steps
 should the IT administrator take to solve the issue?

options.A: Configure the VLAN to split services.
options.B: Route calls through a gigabit port.

explanation: A (Configure the VLAN to split services) is the right move: putting voice on its own VLAN separates it from bulk data traffic and lets QoS prioritize call packets, which is what peak-hour congestion demands. B (Route calls through a gigabit port) does nothing when the bottleneck is the shared ISP link, not the local port speed. C (Shielded cable) addresses electrical interference, not congestion, and D (Increasing the VoIP bit rate) consumes more bandwidth and makes the problem worse.

question:
A user's smartphone frequently disconnects from Wi-Fi networks, particularly in crowded areas like airports and coffee shops. The user also
 notices that their device shows a lower Wi-Fi signal strength compared to other devices in the same location. Which of the following is likely
 contributing to the smartphone's Wi-Fi connectivity issues?

options.A: The smartphone's antenna may be malfunctioning.
options.B: The smartphone may have an outdated Wi-Fi standard.
options.C: The smartphone may be experiencing interference from nearby devices.
options.D: The smartphone's power settings may be affecting performance.

explanation: A (The smartphone's antenna may be malfunctioning) is indicated because the phone shows weaker signal than other devices standing in the same spot - the fault follows the hardware, not the environment. C (Interference from nearby devices) would degrade every device in that airport or coffee shop equally, so it does not explain the discrepancy. B (Outdated Wi-Fi standard) would limit throughput rather than reported signal strength, and D (Power settings) would mainly affect the device when idle or on battery saver.

question: Which of the following internet connection types will most likely experience interference from rain?
explanation: C (Satellite) suffers rain fade: heavy precipitation absorbs and scatters the high-frequency microwave signal travelling between the dish and the orbiting satellite, degrading or dropping the link. A (Fiber) carries light inside glass strands and is immune to weather along its buried or aerial run. B (Cable) uses shielded coax, and D (DSL) uses copper phone lines - both can suffer water ingress at damaged points but are not affected by rainfall itself.

question: A technician is installing an office printer that can only be accessed by a single computer. Which of the following should the technician do?
explanation: A (Configure a USB connection) matches the requirement exactly: a direct USB cable ties the printer to that one workstation and no one else on the network can reach it. C (Set a static IP address) implies putting the printer on the network, which is the opposite of restricting it to a single computer. B (Install a PCL driver) is about page description language and is needed regardless of connection type, and D (Enable secure print) controls job release, not who can connect.

question:
A user reports the following error message to the help desk:
 Drive failure imminent -
 The user presses F1 to continue past the error and work like normal. Which of the following should the help desk technician do to fix this issue?
explanation: A (Replace the hard disk) is correct because Drive failure imminent is a SMART warning generated by the drive's own self-monitoring, meaning it has already logged errors and will fail; back up and swap it. B (Reformat the partition) rewrites the file system but leaves the failing physical media in place. C (Rebuild the array) applies only to a RAID set, which is not indicated here, and D (Enter safe mode) is an OS troubleshooting step that does nothing for firmware-level drive health.

question:
A healthcare facility is printing government documents on preprinted forms. The output has shifted downward on the paper and the printed data is
 not aligned with the blank spaces on the forms. Which of the following should a technician do first?

options.A: Verify that the correct paper type is loaded into the tray.
options.B: Make sure that PostScript drivers are being used.
options.C: Check the orientation settings of the printer.
options.D: Ensure that the pickup rollers are firmly gripping the paper.

explanation: A (Verify that the correct paper type is loaded into the tray) is the first check, because a tray configured or loaded for a different form or size shifts where the printer starts the image, throwing the output off the preprinted fields. C (Check the orientation settings) would produce rotated or sideways output rather than a consistent downward shift. D (Pickup rollers) would cause skew, jams, or misfeeds, and B (PostScript drivers) affects rendering quality, not vertical registration. (Note: the dump prints C as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says A — we go with the community.)

question: Which of the following should a technician check when the display of a computer is flickering?
explanation: B (Refresh rate) is the setting to check: a rate that is too low, or one the panel does not properly support, produces visible flicker, so raising it to the display's native rate normally clears it. C (Screen resolution) mismatches cause blurring, stretching, or black bars, not flicker. A (LCD type) describes the panel technology and is not adjustable, and D (Pixel density) is a fixed physical property of the screen.

question: Which of the following best describes a Type 2 hypervisor?

options.A: It works as a firewall to control network traffic.
options.B: It interacts with the underlying hardware.
options.C: It runs on a host operating system.
options.D: It brings higher CPU capabilities to virtual machines.

explanation: C (It runs on a host operating system) defines a Type 2, or hosted, hypervisor - products like VirtualBox and VMware Workstation install as an application on top of Windows, macOS, or Linux. B (It interacts with the underlying hardware) describes a Type 1 bare-metal hypervisor such as ESXi or Hyper-V, which runs directly on the server with no host OS beneath it. A (Firewall) is a different function entirely, and D is wrong since going through a host OS adds overhead rather than boosting CPU capability.

question:
A user with a home office wants to add additional devices to the existing internet service while maintaining minimal cost and administration.
 Which of the following provides the needed functionality?
explanation: C (Unmanaged switch) is the cheapest, zero-configuration way to turn one existing connection into several ports; plug it in and additional devices join the same network with no administration. A (DSL modem) and D (Cable modem) terminate the ISP circuit, which the user already has, and neither adds usable LAN ports. B (Firewall) adds security functions plus configuration and cost, which conflicts with the minimal-cost, minimal-administration requirement.

question:
A user reports issues controlling the cursor on a company-owned laptop. The technician inspects the laptop and discovers a bulge under the
 trackpad. Which of the following components should the technician replace first?
explanation: C (Battery) should be replaced first: laptop batteries sit directly beneath the palm rest, and a swelling lithium-ion cell pushes up on the trackpad, causing the bulge and erratic or stuck cursor behaviour. It is also a safety issue, so the pack must come out promptly. D (Trackpad) is only being deformed by the pressure and will usually work normally once the battery is removed. A (Motherboard) and B (Heat sink) are elsewhere in the chassis and would not produce a localized bulge.

question:
Which of the following cloud computing models provides hardware, storage, networking, and virtualization, but requires customers to manage the
 OS and applications?
explanation: C (IaaS) delivers the raw building blocks - compute, storage, networking, and the virtualization layer - while the customer installs, patches, and secures the guest operating system and everything above it. B (PaaS) goes further by managing the OS and runtime so the customer only supplies code and data. A (SaaS) provides a complete hosted application with nothing for the customer to maintain, and D (XaaS) is a catch-all umbrella term rather than a specific tier.

question: A user wants a printer set up for scan-to-email functionality. Which of the following should be configured on the printer to fulfill this request?
explanation: B (SMTP) is what scan-to-email needs: the printer acts as a mail client and relays the scanned file to a mail server, so it must be given the SMTP server address, port, and any credentials. D (SMB) is used for scan-to-folder on a Windows share, and C (SFTP) is for scan-to-server file transfer - both deliver files, not messages. A (SMS) is text messaging and has no role in printer scanning.

question: A company wants to share application resources with another business. Which of the following should the company implement?
explanation: A (Community cloud) is infrastructure shared by several organizations with common interests or compliance requirements, which is exactly the arrangement when two businesses pool application resources. B (File synchronization) copies files between devices and does not share applications. C (Rapid elasticity) is the cloud characteristic of scaling capacity on demand, and D (Dedicated resources) means hardware reserved for one tenant - the opposite of sharing with another business.

question:
A technician is installing an expansion card on a desktop computer to provide internet access. Which of the following expansion cards should the
 technician use?
explanation: B (NIC) is the network interface card that gives the desktop an Ethernet or wireless connection for internet access. E (PCIe) is the expansion bus and slot standard the card plugs into, not a card type in itself. A (GPU) drives displays, C (Sound) handles audio input and output, and D (Capture) digitizes incoming video from an external source - none of them provide network connectivity.

question:
An administrator is configuring a SOHO network. The network scope requires static IP addresses for printers. Which of the following must the
 administrator set manually? (Choose two.)
explanation: B (Subnet mask) and C (Default gateway) must be typed in with any static configuration: the mask tells the printer which addresses are local, and the gateway is required for traffic leaving the subnet, such as print jobs from another VLAN. A (DHCP) is the automatic method being replaced. E (Reservations) and F (Exclusions) are DHCP server-side settings, so they are configured on the server rather than on the statically addressed device.

question: A local bank is designing its new infrastructure blueprint. Which of the following RAID types offers double parity?
explanation: D (RAID 6) writes two independent parity blocks striped across the members, so it tolerates two simultaneous drive failures and needs a minimum of four disks. C (RAID 5) has single parity and survives only one lost drive, which is the usual trap here. B (RAID 1) mirrors data with no parity calculation at all, and A (RAID 0) stripes for speed with zero redundancy, so a single failure destroys the set.

question:
A consultant is assessing the wireless configurations for a small office. The existing equipment uses WEP encryption and operates on the default
 channel. The office is in a crowded urban area with many nearby networks. Which of the following is the best way to improve the wireless network
 performance?
explanation: A (Replacing the access point) is the best fix because gear still running WEP is old enough to be limited to 802.11b/g on 2.4GHz; new hardware brings WPA2/WPA3, 5GHz radios, and automatic channel selection that avoids the crowded neighbours. D (Updating the firmware) cannot add radios or standards the hardware lacks. B (Disabling SSID broadcasting) and C (MAC address filtering) are weak security tweaks that do nothing for throughput or channel congestion.

question: Which of the following services allows a networked host to automatically assign IP addresses to devices on a network?
explanation: B (DHCP) hands out IP addresses, along with subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS servers, to clients that request them, leasing each address for a set period. A (DNS) resolves host names to IP addresses that already exist; it does not assign them. C (SMTP) transports email, and D (SNMP) collects management and performance data from network devices - neither has any role in address assignment.

question:
A technician is unable to join a computer to the domain. The technician runs ipconfig and gets the following output:
 Which of the following is the most likely cause?
explanation: D (DNS servers are manually set) is the classic cause: joining a domain requires resolving the SRV records that advertise the domain controllers, and a workstation pointed at a public resolver such as 8.8.8.8 will never find them. It must use the internal Active Directory DNS servers. C (DHCP is enabled) is normal and is actually how clients usually receive the correct internal DNS addresses. A (Subnet mask) errors break general connectivity, and B (NetBIOS) is legacy name resolution that domain join no longer depends on.

question:
A company wants to migrate a large amount of data from an on-premises server to a cloud provider. Which of the following connection types is
 most likely the fastest?
explanation: C (Fiber) offers by far the highest sustained throughput of the WAN options, with symmetrical gigabit or better speeds that suit shipping bulk data to a cloud provider. B (DSL) tops out in the tens of megabits and has very limited upload capacity, while A (Coaxial) cable is faster but still heavily asymmetric, throttling the upstream transfer. D (SAN) is a storage area network inside the data center, not a connection to an external provider.

question:
An end user is having trouble printing from an application. The text on the page is unreadable. However, the application prints successfully from a
 newer computer. Which of the following should be done next?
explanation: C (Update the printer driver) is the next step because garbled or unreadable text is the signature of a wrong or corrupt driver, and the fact that a newer computer prints the same job correctly points at that machine's software rather than the printer. D (Change the toner) would cause faded or streaked output, not scrambled characters. A (Reinstall the printer) is a heavier action to try only if the driver update fails, and B (Adjust the print tray) affects paper handling.

question: Which of the following wireless networking technologies primarily operates in the 5GHz frequency band?
explanation: B (802.11ac) operates exclusively in the 5GHz band, where wider 80 and 160MHz channels and MU-MIMO deliver its high throughput. A (Bluetooth) is a 2.4GHz personal-area technology for short-range device pairing. C (NFC) works at 13.56MHz over a few centimetres, and D (RFID) commonly uses low-frequency, 13.56MHz, or UHF bands around 900MHz for tag reading - none of them are 5GHz.

question: Which of the following cloud characteristics allows local folders to contain updates that are made by users on other devices?
explanation: B (Synchronization) is the cloud characteristic that keeps a local folder matched to the cloud copy, so an edit made on a phone or another PC is pushed down and appears in the same folder everywhere. A (Network share) is a server-hosted folder accessed live over the LAN, with no local synced copy. C (Availability) refers to uptime and accessibility of the service, and D (Metered utilization) is the pay-per-use billing model.

question: Which of the following will most likely be installed in an NVMe port on the motherboard of a desktop PC?
explanation: B (Solid-state drive) is what goes in an NVMe slot - typically an M.2 SSD that talks NVMe directly over PCIe lanes for far lower latency than the older AHCI/SATA path. A (SATA drive) uses the SATA data and power connectors, and although some M.2 slots also accept SATA modules, NVMe specifically means a PCIe SSD. C (SAS drive) is a server interface requiring a SAS controller, and D (Optical drive) connects via SATA.

question:
A desktop support specialist wants to install software that will automatically download email attachments to check for malicious content. Which
 of the following would accomplish this task?
explanation: C (Sandbox) is an isolated, disposable environment where a suspicious attachment can be opened and its behaviour observed without any risk to the production system or network. D (Container) provides process isolation for running applications but shares the host kernel and is built for deployment, not malware detonation. B (Hypervisor) is the underlying platform that could host such an environment rather than the solution itself, and A (VDI) delivers virtual desktops to end users.

question: Which of the following record types is used to create an alias for a domain?
explanation: A (CNAME), the canonical name record, points one hostname at another hostname, which is how aliases such as www are mapped to a primary name. D (A) maps a hostname straight to an IPv4 address and B (AAAA) does the same for IPv6, so both terminate the lookup with an address rather than an alias. C (TXT) holds arbitrary text used for SPF, DKIM, and domain-ownership verification.

question: Which of the following allows an organization to provide remote desktop resources without providing physical workstations to its users?
explanation: C (VDI) hosts each user's desktop as a virtual machine in the data center or cloud, so people connect from thin clients or their own devices and the organization never has to issue physical workstations. A (RMM) is remote monitoring and management tooling technicians use to support endpoints that already exist. B (SaaS) delivers individual hosted applications, not full desktops, and D (Containers) package server applications rather than user desktop sessions.

question: Which of the following is commonly affected by high latency?
explanation: A (Satellite) inherently carries high latency because the signal must travel roughly 22,000 miles up to a geostationary satellite and back on each leg, adding 500ms or more of round-trip delay regardless of bandwidth. That is why it struggles with VoIP, gaming, and remote desktop. B (Fiber), C (Cable), and D (DSL) are all terrestrial links measured in single or low double-digit milliseconds, with DSL degrading over distance but never approaching satellite delay.

question:
A technician must upgrade a computer system to improve its overall processing performance. Which of the following should the technician focus
 on to ensure maximum system performance?
explanation: D (Clock frequency) is the CPU characteristic that most directly raises processing throughput, since more cycles per second means more instructions executed per second. A (Integrated GPU) handles graphics rendering and actually borrows system RAM, doing nothing for general compute. B (Power connectors) simply feed the board and drives, and C (Voltage regulator module) conditions and delivers stable power to the CPU - it supports higher clocks but is not itself a performance upgrade.

question: Which of the following will most likely be an issue when increasing the channel width of an 802.11 network?
explanation: A (Wireless interference) is the trade-off: bonding channels to 40MHz or wider swallows more spectrum, and on 2.4GHz with only three non-overlapping channels the wider channel guarantees it steps on neighbouring networks. B (Decreased data throughput) is backwards - a wider channel raises the potential data rate, which is precisely why people enable it. C (Increased latency) and D (Reduced collisions) are side effects of congestion, not direct results of widening the channel.

question: Which of the following records allow a user to navigate to a server by using a memorable title instead of an IPv4 address? (Choose two.)
explanation: F (A) is the record that maps a host name directly to an IPv4 address, and C (CNAME) is the alias that points a friendly name at another host name, which then resolves through its A record - so both let a user type a name instead of an address. B (AAAA) does the same job for IPv6, not IPv4. A (SPF) and D (TXT) hold text used for mail authentication, and E (MX) directs email to mail servers.

question:
An employee tries to use a projector to share a slideshow from a laptop. The projector displays the message No video signal from source device.
 A technician verifies that all cables are properly connected. Which of the following steps will most likely resolve this issue?

options.D: Putting the slideshow on a USB

explanation: A (Changing the input) is the fix, since No video signal from source device means the projector is watching an input other than the one the laptop is plugged into, or the laptop has not been told to output to an external display. With cables already verified, switching the source is the fastest next step. B (Using a different computer) and D (Putting the slideshow on a USB) are workarounds that skip the actual fault, and C (Power cycling the laptop) is a shot in the dark.

question: Which of the following is the best to use to stream real-time video from a network camera?
explanation: A (UDP) suits real-time video because it is connectionless with no handshake, acknowledgements, or retransmissions - a lost frame is simply skipped rather than resent, which keeps the stream current. B (TCP) guarantees delivery and ordering, but the retransmissions and buffering it needs introduce delay and stalls in a live feed. C (FTP) transfers complete files, and D (RDP) carries remote desktop sessions rather than a camera stream.

question: Which of the following are radio frequency connections? (Choose two.)
explanation: B (Satellite) and D (Cellular) are both radio frequency links: satellite beams microwave signals between a dish and an orbiting relay, and cellular connects handsets to towers over licensed RF spectrum. A (Cable) sends RF-modulated signals but does so inside shielded coaxial copper, so it is a wired service, as is C (DSL) over twisted-pair phone lines. E (Ethernet) is copper cabling and F (Fiber) carries light through glass - none of these three are over-the-air.

question:
An administrator is investigates a misuse of printer resources. The administrator suspects an employee. Which of the following will help the
 administrator verify the source of misuse?
explanation: C (Audit logs) record which user account submitted which job, at what time, and how many pages, which is exactly the evidence needed to tie the misuse to a specific employee. B (Print counter) reports total page volume for the device but not who produced it. A (Secure printing) and D (User authentication) are preventive controls that make future jobs attributable, but on their own they do not provide the historical record for an investigation.

question:
An IT specialist is setting up a new shared network printer. The printer will receive a pre-allocated IP address via DHCP. Attempting to connect to
 the printer's web interface produces a Page not found message. The specialist runs diagnostics and finds that the IP is different than expected.
 Which of the following should the specialist check next?

options.A: The MAC address used in the reservation
options.B: The printer driver on the print server
options.C: The subnet mask that the printer is using
options.D: The default gateway in the address pool

explanation: A (The MAC address used in the reservation) is the thing to check: a DHCP reservation only works if the MAC in the reservation matches the printer's actual interface, and a typo or the wrong NIC means the printer falls back to an ordinary pool address - which is exactly the symptom of getting an unexpected IP. C (Subnet mask) and D (Default gateway) come from the scope and would break routing more broadly. B (Printer driver) affects printing output, not the address the device receives.

question:
A technician must configure a device that can direct packets across multiple broadcast domains. Which of the following devices should the
 technician select?
explanation: D (Router) is the device that forwards packets between separate broadcast domains, making layer 3 decisions based on destination IP and routing tables. A (Switch) forwards frames by MAC address within a single broadcast domain - VLANs create additional domains but a layer 2 switch cannot route between them. B (Modem) converts signals for transmission over an ISP circuit, and C (Access point) bridges wireless clients onto an existing wired segment.

question:
Users in a 200-person call center report that phone calls experience severe performance degradation on busy days. The technician confirms:
 • Upload and download speeds are 50Mbps during a speed test.
 • VoIP call prioritization settings are properly configured for the VLAN that the call center uses.
 Which of the following is most likely the cause of this issue?

options.A: The QoS is not configured correctly on the router.
options.B: The switchports dedicated to the call center are flapping.
options.C: The call center’s VLAN is not configured to allow voice traffic.
options.D: The bandwidth dedicated to the call center is insufficient.

explanation: D (The bandwidth dedicated to the call center is insufficient) is the cause: 50Mbps shared across 200 concurrent agents leaves well under a megabit each, so busy periods saturate the circuit and calls break up. A (QoS) and C (VLAN voice traffic) are ruled out because prioritization on the call center VLAN was verified as correctly configured, and QoS cannot manufacture capacity that is not there. B (Flapping switchports) would cause hard drops and link outages rather than degradation that tracks call volume.

question: Which of the following DNS records is used by DMARC to verify the authenticity of email servers?
explanation: DMARC policies, like SPF and DKIM, are published as C (TXT) records in the domain's DNS zone under _dmarc, telling receiving mail servers how to treat messages that fail authentication. A (MX) only lists the hosts that accept mail for the domain, D (A) maps a hostname to an IPv4 address, and B (CNAME) is an alias pointing at another name - none of them can carry the free-form policy string DMARC needs.

question:
A user reports that when scanning or copying from an MFP, lines appear to be running down the paper. The technician examines the printer and
 determines that it is processing jobs properly. Which of the following should the technician do to resolve this issue?
explanation: Copies and scans are the only jobs that travel across the scanner glass, so dust, toner or correction fluid on the flatbed draws the same line down every captured page while printed jobs stay clean - C (Clean the glass bed) removes it. A (Replace the transfer roller), D (Apply a maintenance kit) and B (Remove the pickup rollers) all address the print engine and paper path, which the technician has already confirmed is processing jobs properly.

question: Which of the following best describes a community cloud?

options.A: Several companies share the same cloud resources.
options.B: Cloud resources are locally hosted in a single company’s data center.
options.C: A third-party provider hosts all cloud resources.
options.D: Some cloud resources are hosted locally while some are hosted by a third-party provider.

explanation: A community cloud is infrastructure shared by several organizations that have common requirements - the same industry, regulator or mission - so they split the cost and the platform between them. B describes a private cloud kept in one company's own data center, C is the public model where a third-party provider owns everything, and D is hybrid, mixing on-premises resources with provider-hosted ones.

question: Which of the following will most likely be used in a testing environment to execute unauthorized code?
explanation: A (Virtual machines) are isolated from the host by the hypervisor and can be snapshotted and rolled back, so untrusted or malicious code can be detonated and observed without touching production - exactly what a sandboxed test environment needs. B (Hybrid cloud) is a deployment model, C (Load balancers) distribute traffic across servers, and D (Application gateways) proxy and filter application traffic; none of them provide a disposable place to run code.

question:
A user's laptop is projecting an image upside down while using a ceiling-mounted projector. Which of the following should a technician do to best
 solve this issue?

options.B: Rotate the image from the laptop.
options.D: Flip the image vertically from the projector.

explanation: Ceiling mounts hang the unit upside down, so projectors include a ceiling or invert mode, and D (Flip the image vertically from the projector) corrects orientation for every device that connects to it. B (Rotate the image from the laptop) fixes only that one machine and leaves the desktop rotated for everyone else who plugs in. A (Change the input source) selects which port is displayed, and C (Adjust the display frequency) changes refresh rate, not orientation.

question:
An administrator selects a new platform that provides the following benefits:
 • Shares a host OS
 • Shares kernel resources
 • Rapid start and deployment
 • Limited isolation
 Which of the following virtualization options did the administrator select?
explanation: B (Containers) package an application with its libraries but run on the host's existing kernel rather than booting a guest OS, which is why they deploy in seconds and give only process-level separation. A (Type 1 hypervisor) and D (Virtual machine) each run a full guest operating system with its own kernel - stronger isolation but slower and heavier. C (Virtual desktop) delivers a user desktop session, not a shared-kernel runtime.

question:
A data center technician notices that one of the servers in a RAID 5 configuration is experiencing slow performance. A message in the server logs
 indicates a degraded RAID array. Which of the following actions should the technician take to address the degraded RAID array?

options.A: Replace the failed drive with a new one.
options.B: Reseat all existing drives to improve connection.
options.C: Perform a disk defragmentation on all drives.
options.D: Change the RAID configuration to RAID 6.

explanation: RAID 5 stripes with distributed parity and tolerates exactly one drive failure, so a degraded array is running with no redundancy left - A (Replace the failed drive with a new one) restores protection by letting the array rebuild before a second disk dies. B (Reseat all existing drives) risks the surviving members, C (disk defragmentation) does nothing for a missing drive, and D (Change to RAID 6) cannot be done on a degraded array and still requires the bad drive replaced.

question:
A user goes to their office and forgets their laptop charger. After borrowing a charger, the user notices that the battery is charging slowly. Which of
 the following steps should a technician take first to charge the battery normally?
explanation: The only thing that changed is the adapter, so the borrowed unit is almost certainly rated for lower wattage or voltage than this laptop draws - C (Use a different power supply) with the correct rating is the quick first test. D (Replace the laptop battery) is expensive and the battery charged normally yesterday, B (Try a different charging port) does not compensate for an underpowered brick, and A (Adjust laptop battery performance) only changes power profiles.

question:
The power supply for a user’s gaming computer fails. The user buys a replacement online. The user connects the power supply to the
 motherboard, the graphics card, and the SSDs, but the computer fails to start and displays a critical error. Which of the following is the most likely
 cause?

options.A: The computer requires an additional RAM upgrade.
options.B: The wattage is insufficient for all the peripherals.
options.C: The user did not connect the 4-pin connector for the CPU.
options.D: The power supply only operates in a redundant configuration.

explanation: Modern boards need the 24-pin main connector plus a separate 4-pin or 8-pin EPS lead dedicated to CPU power; leave C (the 4-pin connector for the CPU) unplugged and the system throws a critical error or will not post even though the GPU and SSDs are wired. B (Insufficient wattage) usually shows as shutdowns under load rather than a dead start, A (RAM upgrade) is unrelated to a PSU swap, and D (redundant configuration) applies to server supplies.

question: A technician must install additional RAM in a desktop computer. Which of the following types of RAM will the technician most likely use?
explanation: Desktop motherboards take C (DIMM) modules - the full-length sticks used by DDR4 and DDR5 in tower systems. B (ECC) and D (Registered) are server-class memory types that most consumer desktop boards and CPUs will not accept, and A (Static) refers to SRAM, which is built into CPU cache rather than sold as installable system memory. DIMM is the form factor the question is after.

question: Which of the following is used to confirm that a physical port is working?
explanation: D (Loopback plug) wires the transmit pins back to the receive pins so the port sends a signal to itself; if the NIC or switch port sees its own traffic, the port and its electronics are good. A (Network tap) copies live traffic for monitoring, C (Patch panel) is a passive termination point in the cabling run, and B (Crimper) attaches connectors to cable ends rather than testing anything.

question:
A user only has access to basic printer functions. A technician notices that the advanced printer features are missing. Which of the following
 actions will fix this issue?

options.A: Modifying the printer settings and rebooting the printer
options.B: Installing the drivers from the printer's manufacturer
options.C: Restarting the OS and attempting to reprint the document
options.D: Applying the OS-provided patches for the printer

explanation: Generic class drivers built into the OS get a printer printing but expose only the basics - duplex, stapling, collation, tray selection and color controls live in the vendor package, so B (Installing the drivers from the printer's manufacturer) restores the advanced options. D (Applying OS-provided patches) just reinstalls that same limited generic driver, and A (Modifying settings and rebooting) or C (Restarting the OS) cannot add features the loaded driver does not implement.

question:
A technician is configuring a desktop computer in a small office. The computer is able to connect to the local file server but is unable to access
 the internet. The technician runs the following command to troubleshoot:
 Which of the following will most likely restore internet access?
explanation: Reaching the local file server proves the address and subnet mask are valid, so traffic only fails when it has to leave the subnet - that is a missing or wrong default gateway, and C (Setting the gateway) restores routing to the internet. A (Flushing the DNS cache) would apply if names failed but IP addresses worked, B (Choosing a different IPv6 address) is irrelevant on an IPv4 LAN, and D (Disabling NetBIOS) affects legacy name resolution, not routing.

question: After replacing a laptop screen, a technician is unable to see Wi-Fi connections. Which of the following will most likely resolve the issue?

options.C: Making sure that all cables are plugged in

explanation: Laptop Wi-Fi antennas run up the display bezel and their thin coax leads plug into the wireless card, so a screen replacement that leaves them unseated kills reception - C (Making sure that all cables are plugged in) is the fix, and it matches the fact that the symptom began right after the repair. A (Turning the Wi-Fi on) ignores that timing, B (Replacing the wireless card) is premature when the card was fine, and D (Disabling WPA) is a security setting.

question:
Which of the following cloud models allows customers to connect to company resources from their laptops with the least amount of
 infrastructure?
explanation: C (SaaS) delivers a finished application over the browser, so users need nothing beyond a laptop and a connection while the provider runs the servers, OS, runtime and software. B (IaaS) hands over raw VMs, storage and networking the customer must build and maintain, A (PaaS) still requires the customer to deploy and manage an application, and D (FaaS) means writing and publishing code rather than simply connecting.

question: Which of the following storage devices is best suited for a high-performance gaming laptop that requires fast data access and transfer rates?
explanation: B (512GB NVMe M.2 SSD) talks to the CPU over PCIe lanes instead of the SATA bus, delivering several gigabytes per second with far lower latency - the load times a gaming laptop needs. A (1TB SATA HDD) and C (750GB SATA III HDD) are mechanical drives limited by platter speed and seek time. D (1TB SAS SSD) is a server interface laptops do not provide, and it is still slower than PCIe.

question: Which of the following will a company most likely use to control which websites a user can access?
explanation: A (Proxy server) sits between users and the internet so every web request passes through it and can be allowed or blocked by URL, category or reputation, which is precisely how site access is controlled. B (Spam gateway) filters inbound email, C (DHCP server) hands out IP configuration, and D (RADIUS server) authenticates users onto the network - none of them decide which pages a browser may load.

question:
After a technician updated the wireless APs to 5GHz, users report they have degraded Wi-Fi performance. The technician tests for interference but
 finds none. Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.B: Switch the Wi-Fi back to the 2.4GHz frequency.
options.C: Upgrade the wireless drivers on the users' devices.
options.D: Add more access points for better coverage.

explanation: 5GHz carries more bandwidth but has shorter range and is absorbed by walls, so AP placement that covered the floor on 2.4GHz now leaves weak spots; D (Add more access points for better coverage) restores what the higher frequency lost. A (Select a different channel) targets interference, which testing already ruled out, B (Switch back to 2.4GHz) abandons the upgrade rather than fixing it, and C (Upgrade the wireless drivers) cannot extend radio range.

question:
An organization upgrades all of its desktop machines to Windows 11. The organization must ensure that all machines are protected from
 malicious software on startup. Which of the following advanced options should the organization enable?
explanation: C (Secure Boot) is the UEFI feature that validates the digital signature of every bootloader and driver before it executes, which stops bootkits and rootkits from loading ahead of Windows at startup. A (Trusted Platform Module) stores keys and boot measurements and backs BitLocker but does not itself refuse unsigned boot code, B (Hardware security module) is a dedicated key-management appliance, and D (BIOS password) only guards firmware settings.

question:
A user reports that the Wi-Fi signal is intermittent in an open office area. Other users are not experiencing this issue. Which of the following is the
 most likely cause?

options.A: There are other Wi-Fi signals that could be causing interference.
options.B: All wireless devices are on the same frequency.
options.C: The laptop's wireless card is malfunctioning.
options.D: The antenna was installed near a device that generates electromagnetic interference.

explanation: The fault follows one machine while everyone else in the same open area is fine, which isolates it to that laptop's own radio, so C (The laptop's wireless card is malfunctioning) is the most likely cause. A (Other Wi-Fi signals causing interference), B (All wireless devices on the same frequency) and D (An antenna near an EMI source) would all degrade every client sharing that space, not a single user's connection.

question:
A Wi-Fi router is set up in a central room. A user on the outer edge of the building reports slow connections and intermittent internet drops. Which
 of the following actions will solve the issue?

options.A: Enabling the 5GHz band from the router configuration page
options.B: Running the flushdns command from the command line
options.C: Upgrading the user’s laptop to a NIC that is compatible with Wi-Fi 6
options.D: Installing additional wireless APs around the location

explanation: The complaint is distance-related - signal falls off toward the building's outer edge - so more coverage is the answer, and D (Installing additional wireless APs around the location) puts a strong signal near that user. A (Enabling the 5GHz band) shortens range further, B (flushdns) only clears cached name lookups, and C (Upgrading to a Wi-Fi 6 NIC) cannot improve a signal that is too weak by the time it arrives.

question:
Faded images from previous jobs appear on each page of output from an office printer. Which of the following should a technician do first to
 resolve this issue?
explanation: Faded repeats of earlier pages are ghosting, caused when toner from the previous image is not fully released and cleared, so C (Inspect the transfer roller) targets the worn or contaminated roller that no longer holds a consistent charge. D (Clean the corona wire) is a follow-up that usually shows as overall faded or blotchy output, B (Adjust the fuser temperature) produces smearing or flaking rather than repeated images, and A (Reload the paper tray) has no bearing on image quality. (Note: the dump prints D as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says C — we go with the community.)

question:
A technician receives a report that the network fileshare has been very slow for several weeks, and today it is no longer available. The file server is
 running, and the technician can establish an RDP connection to it. Which of the following should the technician check next?
explanation: The RDP session proves the network and the OS are healthy, so the failure is confined to the storage holding the share - weeks of gradual slowdown ending in an outage is the classic signature of a failing disk or degraded array, making A (RAID array status) the next check. C (Network connectivity) is already demonstrated by RDP, D (Server available memory) would slow the entire server, and B (Data backup integrity) matters for recovery but diagnoses nothing.

question: Which of the following RAID configurations can lose two drives without data loss?
explanation: D (RAID 6) writes two independent parity blocks across each stripe, so any two members can fail and the data is still rebuildable. C (RAID 5) carries a single parity block and survives only one loss, B (RAID 1) mirrors and tolerates one drive per mirrored pair, and A (RAID 0) is pure striping with no redundancy at all - losing any single drive destroys the whole set.

question: Which of the following technologies is most used in portable devices?
explanation: D (SODIMM) is the small outline memory module made for laptops, mini PCs, printers and other portables where a full-length DIMM will not physically fit. A (ECC) is error-correcting memory aimed at servers and workstations, B (RAID) is a disk redundancy scheme rather than a component, and C (SATA) is a drive interface that portables are steadily replacing with M.2 - none is the memory form factor in question.

question:
A company is installing a new shared printer for all employees in the area. However, some managers need to use the printer for human resources-
 related purposes. The company does not want to purchase additional printers for the private use of the managers. Which of the following should
 the company implement?
explanation: B (Secure printing) holds the job in the device's memory until the person who sent it enters a PIN or badges in at the panel, so HR documents never sit unattended in the output tray of a shared printer. A (Audit logging) records who printed what after the fact but does not protect the page, C (Wired connectivity) is just a transport choice, and D (Duplex settings) only controls two-sided output.

question: Which of the following, when combined, are used to make sure a workstation always has the same IP address on a network managed with DHCP?

options.D: Configuring an automatic private IP address

explanation: C (Assigning a reservation) ties a specific address in the DHCP scope to the workstation's MAC address, so the client leases the same IP every time while remaining centrally managed. A (Creating a new scope) merely defines another pool of dynamic addresses, B (Enabling NAT) translates between private and public addressing, and D (Configuring APIPA) is the 169.254.x.x self-assigned fallback used when no DHCP server responds at all.

question:
A technician is building a home desktop computer. The technician wants to prioritize cable management when considering the type of power
 supply. Which of the following power supply types should the technician consider?
explanation: B (Modular) power supplies let the builder attach only the cables the system actually uses and leave the rest in the box, keeping the case tidy and airflow unobstructed. C (Standard) units have every cable permanently attached, so unused leads must be bundled somewhere inside the chassis. A (Back-up) describes a UPS rather than a PSU type, and D (Redundant) means paired server supplies for uptime, not cable management.

question: Which of the following devices is designed specifically to allow multiple network devices to communicate across a single platform?
explanation: C (Switch) reads the destination MAC address of each frame and forwards it only to the port where that device lives, letting many hosts communicate simultaneously across one platform. D (Routers) work at Layer 3 and join separate networks rather than devices within one, B (Firewall) filters traffic against a rule set, and A (NIC) is just the single interface inside one host.

question:
A client is unable to unlock their smartphone. When they try to enter their code, the input is unsuccessful.
 Which of the following components has most likely failed?
explanation: Entering a passcode depends on the digitizer registering taps, so B (Touch screen) failure means the input never reaches the OS even though the phone is awake and the display looks normal. C (OLED) is the display panel itself - a failure there gives a blank, dim or distorted image rather than dead input. D (Biometric scanner) is bypassed the moment the user chooses to type a code, and A (Charging port) plays no part in touch input.

question: Which of the following supplies power to an IP phone?
explanation: D (PoE switch) injects DC power onto the same twisted pair that carries data, which is how an IP phone runs from a single Ethernet drop with no local adapter. B (Patch panel) is passive copper termination, A (Digital subscriber line) is a WAN access technology over phone lines, and C (Fiber router) may provide the internet circuit but cannot energize a handset over its LAN port.

question:
A company is separating its accounting department’s network from its customer service department’s network.
 Which of the following will accomplish this task?
explanation: C (VLAN) logically divides one physical switch infrastructure into separate broadcast domains, so accounting traffic never reaches the customer service segment and inter-VLAN routing can then be filtered - no extra hardware required. A (VPN) secures remote access across untrusted networks, B (DNS) resolves names to addresses, and D (DHCP) hands out IP configuration; none of them separates two departments.

question:
A mobile user’s laptop is having intermittent performance issues when the user tries to connect to network resources from their desk. Upon
 further research, a technician notices the following:
 • The WLAN signal strength is low within the user’s office.
 • Only two 2.4GHz wireless channels are being used near the user’s office.
 • The user’s laptop was recently imaged, and hardware resources are operating at normal levels.
 • RJ45 ports near the user’s office are not providing any connectivity.
 • The user recently completed several successful password changes.
 • The user is able to connect successfully in other parts of the campus without any performance issues.
 • No other users are experiencing similar issues.
 Which of the following is the most likely cause of the performance issues?

options.A: The APs are installed too far away from the user’s office.
options.B: Multiple brute-force attempts are causing connection drops.
options.C: The ports near the user’s office are currently disabled.
options.D: The user’s laptop has malware, causing it to connect to unauthorized sites.
