explanation: Weak WLAN signal at the desk with only a couple of 2.4GHz channels in use nearby points to a coverage gap rather than congestion, so A (The APs are installed too far away) explains the weak, intermittent connection. B (Brute-force attempts) is contradicted by the successful password changes, C (Disabled ports) explains the dead RJ45 jacks but not the wireless behaviour, and D (Malware) is ruled out by the fresh image and normal resource usage.

question:
A user’s workstation occasionally turns off and smells burnt. The workstation is located in a manufacturing area where users are required to wear
 respirators.
 Which of the following will most likely repair the workstation?

options.A: Inspecting and repairing the swollen motherboard capacitors
options.C: Resetting the BIOS configuration to default

explanation: Respirators mean heavy airborne dust, and a clogged intake filter starves the machine of cooling air until it overheats, shuts down and leaves a burnt smell - so B (Replacing the intake air filter) addresses the actual cause. A (Repairing swollen capacitors) is board-level rework, not a practical field repair. C (Resetting the BIOS to default) changes nothing thermally, and D (Switching the power outlets) would only matter for a power quality fault.

question: Which of the following cables should be installed if nearby electromagnetic interference is a possibility?
explanation: A (STP) wraps foil or braid around the twisted pairs and grounds it, draining motor, fluorescent and other electromagnetic noise away instead of letting it induce onto the conductors. B (UTP) has no shield and is exactly what suffers in a noisy environment. C (Thunderbolt) and D (USB) are short peripheral interfaces, not structured cabling options for a run through an interference-prone area.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic to consider when selecting a satellite internet connection?

options.C: Line of sight to nearby tower

explanation: Signals must travel to orbit and back, so D (Increased latency) is the defining trade-off of satellite service and it hurts VoIP, gaming and remote desktop even when bandwidth looks fine. A (Necessary proximity to urban infrastructure) is backwards, since satellite is chosen precisely for rural sites with no wired options. C (Line of sight to a nearby tower) describes fixed wireless, and B (eSIM requirement) belongs to cellular.

question: Which of the following options offers the best connectivity performance with limited necessary accessories?
explanation: A (Hotspot) uses the cellular radio already built into a phone or dedicated device and shares it over Wi-Fi, giving broadband-class throughput with nothing extra to buy or carry. B (Lightning cable) requires the right cable and a compatible port, D (Bluetooth) tethering runs at a small fraction of that speed, and C (NFC) works only at a few centimetres and exists for pairing and payments, not sustained connectivity.

question:
Users report that multiple desktop computers show the wrong date and time. A technician updates the date and time and restarts the legacy
 system. When the system restarts, the time and date are incorrect again.
 Which of the following should the technician do next to troubleshoot?
explanation: Time that is correct until the machine restarts and then reverts means the coin cell can no longer power the real-time clock while the system is off, so C (Replace the CMOS batteries) is the fix on these legacy desktops. A (Configure the hardware clock) is essentially what the technician already tried, D (Upgrade the NTP settings) would resync after boot but does not explain hardware losing time, and B (Install OS updates) is unrelated.

question:
A technician needs to configure a shared multifunction printer to consume the least amount of supplies.
 Which of the following settings should the technician change?
explanation: D (Duplex configuration) prints on both sides of the sheet, immediately halving the paper consumed by a busy shared MFP. B (Sleep timer) saves electricity rather than supplies, C (Tray settings) only selects which stock is pulled, and A (User authentication) can discourage casual printing but does not reduce the consumables used by each job the way two-sided output does.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting an MFP issue in which the printed copies have speckling. The technician verifies that the issue does not occur
 when a document is scanned, but speckling does appear when copied. After verifying that the print does not smear on the page after printing,
 which of the following should the technician do to fix the issue?
explanation: Clean scans prove the scanner path is fine, so the defect is added during printing, and the absence of smearing rules out fusing - that leaves residual toner being deposited by a contaminated transfer roller, so D (Clean the transfer roller) is the fix. C (Replace the print fuser) is contradicted by the lack of smudging, B (Change the toner cartridge) addresses fading and streaking, and A (Install a maintenance kit) is a bigger service action to try later.

question:
When a user scans a page on a printer, a line always appears on the printout. However, when the user prints from the printer, the line does not
 appear.
 Which of the following maintenance steps should a technician take to resolve the issue?
explanation: Only scanned output carries the line, so the mark is introduced in the optical path rather than the print engine - dirt or a scratch on the flatbed puts a streak on every captured image, and B (Wipe the flatbed glass) clears it. C (Remove any internal debris) and D (Clean the heating element) target printer components that are already producing clean pages, and A (Replace the paper type) cannot change what the scanner sees.

question: Which of the following requires pairing during the initial use of a new mobile accessory?
explanation: D (Bluetooth) requires a pairing exchange the first time two devices meet - they discover each other, confirm a code, and store a link key so later connections happen automatically. A (NFC) and C (RFID) work by tap-and-read at a few centimetres with no persistent pairing relationship, and B (Lightning cable) is a wired connection that simply works the moment it is plugged in.

question:
Which of the following networking technologies allows for high-speed data transmission over short distances between devices like smartphones
 and tablets?
explanation: D (Wi-Fi Direct) lets two devices negotiate a direct 802.11 link without an access point, so a phone and tablet get Wi-Fi-class throughput across a room. A (Near-field communication) tops out near 424 kbps at a few centimetres and is meant for tap actions, C (Infrared) is slow and needs unobstructed line of sight, and B (Zigbee) is a deliberately low-power, low-data-rate mesh for IoT sensors.

question:
A user reports that their smartphone requires frequent charging. The user purchased the smartphone new three years ago, and it would last a full
 day on a single charge. The user now keeps application usage to a minimum and enables power efficiency modes to prolong the smartphone’s
 charge. A technician connects the smartphone to a cable and notices it takes much longer to fully charge the battery than the manufacturer’s
 specifications.
 Which of the following should the technician check for next?
explanation: Charge time far outside the manufacturer's specification points at the power path rather than capacity, so A (Damaged ports) is the next thing to inspect - lint, corrosion or bent pins in the connector throttle the current the phone can draw. C (Performance degradation) is the ageing already described rather than a new check, B (Malware infection) drains a battery but does not slow charging, and D (Overheating) would present as a hot device and throttling.

question:
A user’s smartphone frequently disconnects from Wi-Fi networks, particularly in crowded areas like airports and coffee shops. The user also
 notices that their device shows a lower Wi-Fi signal strength compared to other devices in the same location.
 Which of the following is likely contributing to the smartphone’s Wi-Fi connectivity issues?

options.A: The smartphone’s antenna may be malfunctioning.
options.B: The smartphone may have an outdated Wi-Fi standard.
options.C: The smartphone may be experiencing interference from nearby devices.
options.D: The smartphone’s power settings may be affecting performance.

explanation: Other devices standing in the same spot report stronger signal, which isolates the fault to this handset's radio hardware, so A (The smartphone's antenna may be malfunctioning) explains both the weak reading and the drops. C (Interference from nearby devices) and B (An outdated Wi-Fi standard) would affect other clients too or cap throughput without lowering measured signal strength, and D (Power settings) changes battery-saving behaviour, not reception.

question:
Some users are unable to access their workstations. An administrator runs ipconfig on one of the workstations and sees the following:
 IPv4 address: 192.168.1.27 -
 Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0 -
 Default gateway: 192.168.1.1 -
 The administrator runs the following command and receives this output:
 C:\Users\User> ping gateway -
 Pinging gateway (192.168.1.1) with 32 bytes of data:
 Request timed out.
 Request timed out.
 Request timed out.
 Request timed out.
 Which of the following is the source of issue?
explanation: The workstation holds a valid address on the same subnet as 192.168.1.1 and the name even resolves, yet the first hop never answers, so B (Router) - the default gateway device - is down or has failed. C (DNS) clearly worked because the name resolved to the correct address, D (DHCP) delivered a correct address, mask and gateway, and A (Web server) sits far beyond a hop that is already failing.

question:
A user’s laptop experiences intermittent issues during startup. A technician finds that the user has left a corporate flash drive plugged in, which is
 causing the issues. Which of the following should the technician configure?
explanation: The firmware is trying to boot from the flash drive because removable media sits ahead of the internal disk in the boot order, so B (Boot options) in UEFI is what needs correcting. C (USB Enable) would disable USB devices altogether, which is heavy-handed, A (BitLocker) encrypts the volume, and D (TPM features) manage keys and measured boot - none of them changes which device the system tries first.

question: Which of the following protocol ports is used for secure remote access to a network device?
explanation: B (22) is SSH, which encrypts the entire management session and is the standard way to reach switches, routers and servers remotely. C (23) is Telnet, functionally similar but sending credentials and commands in clear text, A (21) is the FTP control channel for file transfer, and D (25) is SMTP for moving mail between servers - neither is remote administration.

question: Which of the following statements is true when comparing DDR3 RAM and DDR4 RAM?

options.A: DDR4 offers faster data transfer rates compared to DDR3.
options.B: DDR3 is capable of achieving higher bandwidth than DDR4.
options.C: DDR4 operates at a higher voltage than DDR3.
options.D: DDR3 is better suited for low-power environments than DDR4.

explanation: A is correct because DDR4 raised base clocks and transfer rates well beyond DDR3, starting around 2133 MT/s and climbing from there. B reverses the bandwidth relationship, C is wrong on voltage since DDR4 dropped to 1.2V from DDR3's 1.5V, and D follows from that same point - the lower-voltage DDR4 is the better fit for low-power laptops and mobile systems, not DDR3.

question: Which of the following devices forwards data between different networks by analyzing the headers of packets?
explanation: B (Router) works at Layer 3, reading the destination IP in each packet header and consulting its routing table to forward the packet toward the correct network. A (Hub) and C (Repeater) simply regenerate the electrical signal at Layer 1 with no addressing awareness, and D (Unmanaged switch) forwards frames by MAC address within a single network without ever inspecting IP headers.

question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of cloud computing that ensures resources are dynamically distributed to meet varying workloads?
explanation: B (Elasticity) is the ability to add and release compute, storage or bandwidth automatically as demand rises and falls, so capacity tracks the workload in real time. D (Metered utilization) is the pay-per-use billing model that makes elasticity affordable but performs no scaling, C (Multitenancy) means several customers share the same underlying hardware, and A (Hybrid deployment) simply describes where resources are located.

question:
A customer experiences a power outage at their data center. After the outage, one server with three hard drives in RAID 5 does not come back
 online. When a technician connects to the server, they receive a message stating that Drive 3 has failed. Which of the following steps should the
 technician take next to minimize the risk of data loss?

options.A: Replace the defective drive and trigger an array rebuild.
options.B: Acknowledge the drive error and allow the system to start normally.
options.C: Upgrade the firmware on the drives.
options.D: Perform a full drive restore from the most recent backup.

explanation: Three drives in RAID 5 with one member failed means the array is degraded and running on parity, so a second failure loses everything - A (Replace the defective drive and trigger an array rebuild) restores redundancy while it is still possible. B (Acknowledge the error and start normally) leaves the data exposed, D (Full restore from backup) discards current data unnecessarily, and C (Upgrade the firmware) does nothing about a missing disk.

question:
An end user is printing, but the image is being cut off because the paper is too small. The user did put the correct type of paper in the printer.
 Which of the following should the user change first?
explanation: The correct stock is already loaded, so the mismatch is on the document side - the image is scaled larger than the sheet, and A (The image size) or a scale-to-fit setting brings it inside the printable area. C (The tray settings) would matter only if the wrong paper were being pulled, which the scenario rules out. B (The quality of the image) changes DPI, and D (The file type) changes format; neither crops the page.

question:
A technician connects a network printer to a SOHO router. The technician configures several workstations to send print jobs to the printer's
 network address. After several days, users report that they are no longer able to use the printer. Which of the following should the technician use
 to resolve the issue and prevent it from reoccurring?
explanation: The printer was reached at a DHCP-assigned address, and when that lease expired it picked up a different one while the workstations kept pointing at the old address - D (Static IP), or an equivalent DHCP reservation, pins it permanently. A (Network gateway) has no bearing on how clients locate the printer, B (USB cable) abandons network printing entirely, and C (APIPA) is the 169.254 self-assigned fallback, which would make things worse.

question:
A user reports issues trying to print to a printer. Every time the user tries to print, continuous pages of random characters are printed. There are no
 smudging or print quality issues. Which of the following should the technician do to resolve this issue?
explanation: Pages of random characters mean the printer is receiving a data stream in a language it cannot interpret, so it prints the raw code instead of rendering the page - A (Reinstall the printer driver software) replaces the wrong or corrupted driver behind it. The absence of smudging or quality defects rules out C (Replace the toner cartridge), B (Configure DPI settings) only changes resolution, and D (Update firmware) is a heavier step to try afterwards.

question: A business purchases a computer with a built-in WWAN card. Which of the following technologies does the computer's WWAN card support?
explanation: A WWAN card is a cellular modem, so it needs carrier credentials supplied by A (SIM), whether that is a physical card or an embedded eSIM, before it can attach to the mobile network. D (Wi-Fi) is WLAN and runs on a separate radio, C (Bluetooth) is a personal-area link measured in metres, and B (NFC) operates at a few centimetres for tap interactions.

question:
An end user is able to send emails but not receive them. Which of the following settings should a technician check first on the user's laptop to
 troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: Outbound mail works, so the sending path is proven and the fault lies in retrieval - C (IMAP), on port 143 or 993 with TLS, is what pulls messages down from the server, and a wrong server name, port or credential there stops incoming mail. B (SMTP) covers the outbound side that already works, A (DNS) failure would break both directions, and D (DMARC) is a domain authentication policy, not a client setting.

question:
An office manager wants to know which users are printing the most pages. Which of the following can a technician enable to provide this data to
 the office manager?
explanation: A (Audit logging) on the printer or print server records every job with the submitting user, timestamp and page count, which is exactly the per-user report the office manager is asking for. B (Control language) refers to PCL or PostScript, the way pages are described to the device, C (Firmware updates) patches the printer, and D (Network scan services) sends scans to email or a file share.

question: Which of the following cloud models allows an organization to have exclusive access to cloud resources?
explanation: C (Private) dedicates the infrastructure to a single organization, whether it sits in that company's own data center or is hosted for them, so no other tenant shares those resources - the model chosen for strict control and compliance. A (Public) is multitenant by design, D (Community) shares among several organizations with common needs, and B (Hybrid) deliberately combines private and public capacity.

question:
Which of the following cloud models allows for some services to remain on premises and other services to be delivered by a cloud-hosting
 provider?
explanation: A (Hybrid) links an organization's on-premises or private infrastructure to public cloud services, so each workload can sit wherever it fits best and can burst or migrate between the two. D (Private) keeps everything on dedicated infrastructure, C (Public) puts everything at the provider, and B (Community) is shared infrastructure for a group of organizations rather than a mix of local and hosted services.

question: Which of the following allows an internal application to be hosted without managing the underlying OS?
explanation: D (PaaS) supplies the OS, runtime and middleware as a managed platform, so developers just deploy their application code while the provider patches, secures and scales everything underneath. B (IaaS) hands over virtual machines the customer must still maintain, A (SaaS) is a finished application with nowhere to host your own, and C (UCaaS) delivers hosted voice, messaging and conferencing services.

question:
A customer's laptop is no longer charging when plugged in to the docking station. A technician observes that none of the devices plugged in to
 the dock appear to be functioning. The technician verifies that the dock has power, the laptop ports are not damaged, and the BIOS updates are
 current, but the issue persists. Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.B: Replace the dock with a new one.
options.C: Reinstall the OS on the laptop.

explanation: Nothing attached to the dock works, not just charging, and the dock's power, the laptop ports and the firmware have all been verified - the only untested component left is the dock, so B (Replace the dock with a new one) is the next step. A (Switch the power supply) is covered by confirming the dock has power, D (Roll back the BIOS updates) undoes a current, correct update, and C (Reinstall the OS) cannot explain a hardware-wide dock failure.

question:
A technician is installing a new speaker and microphone in a conference room. The technician makes the connections and installs the
 manufacturer's application for the devices. However, when the technician uses corporate collaboration tools, the input and output devices have
 not switched to the new speaker and microphone. Which of the following should the technician do to ensure that the new conference devices are
 working properly?

options.A: Configure the default devices in the meeting software sound settings.
options.B: Install the proper drivers for the devices.
options.C: Disable the speaker and microphone in the computer’s BIOS.
options.D: Power cycle the devices and the laptop.

explanation: Collaboration and meeting applications keep their own audio device selection independent of Windows, so the software is still pointed at the built-in speaker and mic; setting the new hardware as the default input and output inside the meeting software's sound settings is what switches it. B (Install the proper drivers) is already done, since the manufacturer's application installed and the devices connected. D (Power cycle) will not change a saved application preference, and C (Disable in BIOS) removes hardware rather than selecting it.

question:
A user's laptop monitor dims every evening. The user manually adjusts the screen setting but wants a permanent solution. Which of the following
 settings should a technician change to prevent the issue?
explanation: Adaptive or ambient light brightness uses the light sensor to dim the panel as the room gets darker, which is why it happens every evening; turning that setting off makes the manual brightness stick. B (Battery) settings dim the screen on low charge or when unplugged, not at a particular time of day. C (Graphics) controls resolution, refresh rate and color profiles, and D (Scheduled tasks) does not manage display brightness.

question:
A help desk technician investigates a laser printer issue. Smudges are appearing on the printed pages, but they are not present on the document
 that was sent to the printer. Which of the following should the technician do first to diagnose the issue?

options.A: Use a different kind of printing paper.

explanation: Smudging that appears only on the printed output points at the imaging path, and the drum is the component that transfers toner to the page, so a scratched, worn or contaminated drum deposits toner where it should not be. Inspecting it is a diagnostic step that costs nothing. A (Different paper) and D (Replace the toner) are parts swaps done before the cause is known, and C (Update the firmware) cannot produce physical marks on paper.

question: Which of the following controls network traffic based on MAC addresses?
explanation: A switch is a Layer 2 device: it builds a MAC address table from the source addresses of incoming frames and forwards each frame only out the port where that MAC lives. A (Router) makes forwarding decisions on IP addresses at Layer 3, between networks. C (Firewall) filters on IP addresses, ports and rules rather than hardware addresses, and B (PoE injector) only adds DC power to an Ethernet run.

question:
A thief stole a company phone and successfully extracted confidential company information from the device. Which of the following should have
 been used to prevent the extraction?
explanation: Mobile device management enforces the controls that make a stolen handset useless: full-device encryption, mandatory screen lock, and remote lock or remote wipe once the loss is reported. A (GPS) can locate the phone but does nothing to keep data from being pulled off it. B (EFS) is Windows Encrypting File System, not a mobile technology, and C (eSIM) is just a carrier-provisioning method for the cellular subscription.

question:
A user has two SSDs of the same size in their PC. The user wants to configure both SSDs to have a copy of all data so there will be no data loss if
 one drive fails. Which of the following is this an example of?
explanation: RAID 1 mirrors, writing identical data to both drives so the array keeps running on one disk if the other dies, which is exactly two same-size SSDs holding a full copy each. A (RAID 0) stripes for speed with no redundancy at all, and losing either drive loses everything. C (RAID 5) needs a minimum of three drives for striping with parity, and D (RAID 10) needs at least four.

question: The display in a conference room has a burn-in that does not match the presentation. Which of the following would best resolve the issue?
explanation: Burn-in is permanent physical degradation of the panel, where pixels that displayed a static image retain a ghost of it; no configuration change reverses that, so the display has to be replaced. A (Color settings) and C (Increase brightness) at best make the ghost image less obvious and often make it more visible. B (Correct the keystone) is a projector geometry adjustment for a trapezoid image, an unrelated symptom.

question:
A technician needs to provide a new employee with a phone number for their company mobile phone number. Which of the following is the most
 cost-effective and professional way to complete this task?

options.A: Forward a company number to the employee's mobile phone.
options.B: Offer a company SIM card to the employee.
options.C: Give a company mobile phone to the employee.
options.D: Issue a company eSIM to the employee.

explanation: An eSIM is provisioned digitally by the carrier and downloaded straight to the handset, so the employee gets a company-owned number immediately with no hardware to buy, ship or install, and the line stays under corporate control. B (Company SIM card) means procuring and mailing a physical card. C (Give a company mobile phone) is the most expensive option by far, and A (Forwarding a number) only redirects inbound calls, leaving the personal number exposed on outbound ones.

question:
A user asks a technician to increase the storage capacity of their new laptop by adding another SSD. Which of the following connectors will the
 technician most likely use?
explanation: Internal 2.5in laptop drive bays connect over SATA, so a technician adding a second SSD to an existing bay uses a SATA data and power connection. A (USB) would make it an external drive, not an internal capacity upgrade. C (SAS) is a server and enterprise storage interface not found in laptops, and D (SCSI) is a legacy parallel standard long retired from consumer systems.

question:
A technician adds the NTP service to a server and configures all network computers to that service. Which of the following is the technician most
 likely trying to achieve?

options.B: Enabled print services on the server

explanation: Network Time Protocol distributes accurate time from a reference source over UDP 123, so pointing every computer at the new service keeps all system clocks in agreement, which matters for authentication tickets, certificates and log correlation. A (Transport protocols) and B (Print services) have nothing to do with NTP. D (DHCP server options) can hand out the NTP server's address, but that is the delivery mechanism, not the goal being achieved.

question: Which of the following best describes the benefits of cloud computing in the context of business operations?

options.A: It provides elasticity, allowing businesses to scale resources up or down easily.
options.B: It offers complete control over physical servers to the IT team.
options.C: It removes the need for software licenses for on-premises deployments.
options.D: It delivers on-premises data storage for sensitive information.

explanation: Elasticity is the defining business benefit: capacity is added or removed on demand and billed by consumption, so a company sizes for real load instead of buying hardware for peak. B (Control over physical servers) describes on-premises infrastructure, and cloud deliberately abstracts that away. C (No software licenses) is false, subscriptions and licensing still apply, and D (On-premises storage) is the opposite of a cloud service.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a Type 1 hypervisor?
explanation: A Type 1 hypervisor installs directly onto bare metal and acts as the operating system itself, managing hardware and guests with no layer beneath it, which is why it delivers better performance and isolation on servers. A (Host OS required) describes a Type 2 hosted hypervisor such as VirtualBox or VMware Workstation. C (Lightweight OS) and D (Local configuration options) are vague traits that do not distinguish the two types.

question:
A marketing developer creates a new DNS record called promotions.comptia.org so it references the same IP address as www.comptia.org. Which
 of the following DNS records did the developer change in this scenario?
explanation: A CNAME creates an alias, pointing promotions.comptia.org at the canonical name www.comptia.org so it resolves to whatever address that host currently uses. C (A record) would hardcode the IP address into a second record, meaning two places to update whenever the server moves. A (MX) directs mail to a mail exchanger, and D (TXT) stores free-form text used for SPF and domain verification.

question:
A technician is evaluating how to connect a power-redundant server to the outlets of a rack. Which of the following is the best way to provide
 electricity to the server?

options.A: Using only one power outlet, as the system will provide energy to the redundant source
options.B: Leaving one of the power supplies disconnected for use in case the other fails
options.C: Identifying available power outlets in different UPSs and distributing the connection between them
options.D: Connecting the device to one dedicated battery backup to provide continuous energy

explanation: Dual power supplies only buy redundancy if each one is fed from an independent source, so plugging them into outlets on two different UPS units removes the single point of failure. A (One outlet) leaves the whole server dependent on one feed, and D (One dedicated battery backup) has the same flaw. B (Leaving a supply disconnected) defeats the automatic failover entirely, since nobody is there to plug it in at the moment of failure.

question: Which of the following cables can carry a video signal?
explanation: USB-C carries video through DisplayPort Alternate Mode or Thunderbolt, letting a single cable drive a monitor along with data and power. A (MicroUSB), B (USB-A) and C (MiniUSB) are data and power connectors with no video pins or alternate mode support, so driving a display from them requires an active adapter with its own display chipset rather than the cable itself.

question: A user asks a technician to recommend a CPU upgrade for a desktop computer. Which of the following should the technician consider first?
explanation: The processor must physically fit the board's socket and be supported by that chipset and BIOS version, so socket compatibility is the gate that everything else passes through; a faster chip in the wrong socket simply cannot be installed. A (Core count), C (Bus frequency) and D (Integrated GPU) all matter when picking between the parts that do fit, but they are performance considerations that come after compatibility is confirmed.

question: Which of the following is used to verify the functionality of an Ethernet NIC?
explanation: A loopback plug wires the transmit pins back to the receive pins so the NIC sends a signal and immediately receives its own traffic, confirming the port and adapter work independently of the cable plant. A (Toner probe) traces and locates cable runs. C (Wi-Fi analyzer) surveys wireless channels and signal strength, and D (Punchdown tool) seats conductors into a 66 or 110 block.

question: A small office is using an internal subnet that includes 192.168.1.0 through 192.168.1.255. Which of the following is the proper subnet mask?
explanation: 192.168.1.0 through 192.168.1.255 is a single 256-address block, which is a /24, and 255.255.255.0 is that mask: the first three octets identify the network and the last is free for hosts. D (255.255.255.128) is a /25 and would split the range into two halves of 128. B (255.0.0.0) is a /8 covering far more, and A (0.0.0.0) is not a usable host mask.

question:
A user is setting up a gaming PC with multiple GPUs to play highly advanced games. The user's primary concern is that the power supply is
 sufficient to support these tasks while allowing for future upgrades. Which of the following power supply configurations should the user select?
explanation: A multiple-rail supply splits its 12V output across several rails, each with its own over-current protection, so the load from several power-hungry GPUs is distributed safely instead of riding one rail, and there is headroom for more cards later. A (Redundant) supplies are for servers needing failover, not gaming throughput. B (Non-modular) only describes fixed cabling, and C (Low wattage) is the opposite of what multiple GPUs need.

question: A technician needs to run cable for a new office through a drop ceiling. Which of the following cable types should the technician run?
explanation: Drop ceilings are air-handling plenum spaces, and fire code requires cable run there to use a plenum-rated jacket such as FEP that resists flame and gives off little toxic smoke. B (Fiber-optic) and C (Coaxial) describe the media rather than the fire rating, and both are also sold in plenum and non-plenum versions. A (BNC) is a connector type, not a cable rating.

question:
An administrator for a wireless network is planning the company’s floor plan using a heat map. Which of the following types of networks is the
 administrator configuring?
explanation: A heat map plots wireless signal strength and coverage across a floor plan, which is a wireless LAN survey used to place access points and find dead spots. A (SAN) is a dedicated block-level storage network. B (PAN) covers a few metres around one person, such as Bluetooth peripherals, and C (MAN) spans a city, neither of which is planned per floor with a coverage map.

question:
A technician recently replaced a user's laptop screen. Since then, the user has had trouble connecting to wireless networks. Which of the following
 should the technician do?

options.A: Verify that wireless technologies are compatible with the updated hardware.
options.B: Reinstall the wireless drivers after the OS is reloaded.
options.C: Reconnect the antenna to the system board.

explanation: Laptop Wi-Fi antennas run up the sides of the display panel and connect down through the hinge to the wireless card, so a screen replacement is the classic reason they end up unseated or pinched. B (Reinstall drivers after OS reload) and D (Reset network services) address software when the timing points squarely at the physical work. A (Compatibility) is not a factor, since a replacement screen does not change the wireless standard supported.

question:
A technician builds a workstation. When the technician starts up the workstation, the technician notices a burning smell. During POST, the
 workstation shuts down. Which of the following is most likely the cause of these issues?

options.A: The technician did not properly ground the workstation.
options.B: The technician chose the wrong type of RAM.
options.C: The technician did not connect power to the exhaust fan.
options.D: The technician did not apply thermal paste.

explanation: Without thermal paste there is no heat transfer between the CPU die and the heat sink, so the core spikes to its thermal limit within seconds and the board shuts down mid-POST, with the smell coming from the overheating components. B (Wrong RAM) prevents POST from completing but produces beep codes, not heat. C (Unpowered exhaust fan) causes gradual heat buildup rather than an immediate POST shutdown, and A (Improper grounding) causes ESD damage.

question:
A device with an IP address of 169.254.34.24 is having trouble accessing internet websites. Which of the following is most likely causing the
 issue?

options.A: The static IP address configuration is incorrect.
options.C: The DHCP assignment cannot be obtained.
options.D: The internet is disconnected from the router.

explanation: 169.254.x.x is an APIPA address, which a Windows client assigns itself only after its DHCP requests go unanswered, so the device never got a lease and has no gateway or DNS to reach the internet. A (Incorrect static IP) is ruled out because a manually configured host keeps the address it was given. B (DNS failure) would still allow access by IP, and D (Router internet down) would not stop DHCP from issuing a normal lease.

question:
An office manager wants to scan a contract that is approximately 300 pages. The office manager is concerned the process will take a long time
 because each page must be scanned individually. Which of the following can the office manager use to increase the speed of scanning?
explanation: An automatic document feeder pulls a stack of pages through the scanner one after another without anyone lifting a lid, which is the only option here that removes the per-page handling on a 300-page contract. A (Flatbed) is exactly the manual method causing the complaint. B (Duplexing) captures both sides of a sheet but is a feature of the feeder, and D (Orientation) only affects how the image is rotated.

question:
Which of the following internet connection types is primarily used for high-speed internet access in rural areas where traditional broadband
 services are unavailable?
explanation: Satellite service needs only a dish with a clear view of the sky, so it reaches remote properties where no cable plant exists, at the cost of high latency and weather sensitivity. A (Fiber) and D (Cable) require the provider to trench and build out infrastructure that rural areas usually lack. C (DSL) rides existing telephone copper but degrades badly with distance from the central office.

question: Which of the following cloud delivery models should an organization choose when it requires ownership of all physical hardware?
explanation: A private cloud is single-tenant infrastructure dedicated to one organization, which is the only model that lets that organization own and physically control every piece of hardware. C (Public cloud) runs on shared provider-owned equipment, and A (Hybrid cloud) by definition includes that public component. D (IaaS) and E (PaaS) are service models describing what is delivered, not who owns the underlying hardware.

question: Which of the following devices can handle large volumes of data and uses flash memory?
explanation: An SSD stores data in NAND flash with no moving parts, giving high capacity with fast random access and low power draw. C (HDD) holds large volumes too but uses spinning magnetic platters and read/write heads. B (DVD-RW) is optical media limited to a few gigabytes, and D (Tape) is high-capacity magnetic media but strictly sequential, which suits archival backup rather than general use.

question:
A programmer needs to run a virtual machine on their laptop to test an application. Which of the following virtualization technologies is the best
 way to accomplish this goal?
explanation: A hypervisor, specifically a Type 2 hosted product running on top of the laptop's existing OS, creates a virtual machine with its own guest operating system and virtual hardware, which is what testing an application in isolation needs. A (Containerization) shares the host kernel and packages an app rather than a full OS. C (VDI) hosts desktops centrally in a data center, and D (Emulation) reproduces a different CPU architecture and runs far slower.

question:
A company wants to optimize its hardware usage by running multiple operating systems concurrently on a single physical server. Which of the
 following concepts achieves this goal?
explanation: Host-based virtualization puts a hypervisor on the one physical server and partitions its CPU, memory and storage among several guest operating systems running side by side, which is precisely how idle hardware capacity gets reclaimed. C (High-availability clustering) links multiple nodes for failover rather than consolidating onto one, and E (Load balancing) spreads traffic across servers. B (Public cloud) and D (SaaS) move the workload off the company's hardware entirely.

question:
A network printer consistently produces faint printouts. Users report that the issue persists across different computers and print jobs. Which of
 the following steps should the technician take first?
explanation: Consistently faint output that follows the printer across every computer and job is a consumable problem, and low toner is the first and cheapest thing to swap. C (Reinstall the drivers) is ruled out because the fault would then be limited to one workstation, not shared by all. A (Calibration) corrects color registration and alignment, and D (Fuser temperature) shows up as toner smearing or flaking off, not as uniformly pale pages.

question:
A user turns on their laptop. The keyboard lights up. but the screen is black even after the user restarts the laptop. Which of the following should a
 technician do next to troubleshoot the issue?

options.A: Connect the laptop to an external monitor.

explanation: Attaching an external monitor splits the fault in one step: an image on the external display isolates the problem to the panel, backlight or video cable, while a black external screen points at the GPU or system board. B (Remove the bezel) is invasive disassembly before the fault is localised. C (Plug in the charger) is pointless since the keyboard backlight shows the system has power, and D (Replace the laptop) skips troubleshooting altogether.

question: A user reports that the office inkjet printer is making smudges on the printed pages. Which of the following tasks would best resolve the issue?
explanation: Inkjet smudging comes from clogged or crusted print head nozzles spraying ink unevenly, and running the printer's head cleaning utility clears the dried ink. A (Maintenance kit) and D (Replace the fuser) are laser printer procedures, and an inkjet has no fuser because it does not use heat to bond toner. C (Clear jams) addresses misfeeds and paper tearing, which are not what is being reported.

question:
Marketing department users report network performance degradation in the morning and early afternoon, but sales and customer service
 department users do not report any issues. All structured cabling is Cat 5e. All departments are connected to a core switch. The running network
 configuration shows the following:
 Which of the following is the most likely cause of the performance issues?

options.A: The marketing department subnet has an error.
options.B: The structured Cat 5e cabling is outdated.
options.C: The interfaces are configured with incorrect IP addresses.
options.D: The marketing department interface is running at 10/100.

explanation: The marketing interface negotiated at 10/100 while the rest of the network runs gigabit, so that link saturates as soon as the department gets busy, which matches slowdowns confined to peak morning and afternoon hours. B (Cat 5e) is not the limit, since 5e carries gigabit comfortably over standard runs. A (Subnet error) and C (Incorrect IP addresses) would break connectivity outright rather than allow normal use that merely gets slow under load.

question:
A user needs cellular internet connectivity for their laptop without using an external device. Which of the following technologies can the user use
 on their laptop to achieve this connection?
explanation: A laptop with an integrated WWAN module takes a carrier SIM and connects directly to the cellular network, satisfying the requirement that no external device be involved. B (Hotspot) works but depends on a phone or dedicated device sharing its connection, which is the external device the user is trying to avoid. A (Bluetooth) and D (NFC) are short-range personal-area technologies that provide no internet access on their own.

question:
A company wants to get the fastest network speeds possible between nearby locations. If all technologies are available, which of the following
 connection types should the company use?
explanation: Fiber offers the highest bandwidth and lowest latency of the options, and it carries light rather than electrical signals, so it runs long distances between sites without attenuation or interference. B (DSL) is capped by copper loop length. C (Satellite) adds hundreds of milliseconds of latency from the round trip to orbit, and D (Coaxial) is shared bandwidth with far lower upstream capacity.

question: Which of the following describes an advantage of traditional HDDs over SSDs?
explanation: Cost per gigabyte is where mechanical drives still win: spinning platters deliver far more capacity per dollar, which is why bulk storage, backups and archives still lean on them. A (Faster access) is plainly an SSD advantage, since flash has no seek time. B (Energy efficiency) and D (Lower weight and size) also favour SSDs, which have no motor, platters or actuator arm to drive.

question:
After a laptop screen has been replaced, the laptop is having Wi-Fi connectivity issues. No SSIDs are discovered. Bluetooth and Ethernet are
 working. Which of the following should a technician investigate first?
explanation: The wireless antennas are routed through the display assembly, so a screen replacement is the likely reason the card can no longer hear any beacons and shows zero SSIDs. A (Wireless card) is less likely because Bluetooth commonly shares that same card and still works, indicating the radio is alive but deaf. C (Wireless AP) would affect every device in the office, and D (NIC) and E (Motherboard) are ruled out by working Ethernet.

question: Which of the following is used to assign an IP address to a network PC?
explanation: DHCP leases IP addresses along with subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server settings, automating what would otherwise be manual configuration on every host. B (DNS) resolves hostnames to addresses already assigned. A (VLAN) logically segments switch ports into separate broadcast domains, and D (TCP) is the transport protocol that carries the session once the host already has an address.

question: Which of the following offers access to business productivity applications for a recurring fee?
explanation: Software as a Service delivers finished applications such as email, office suites and CRM over the internet on a subscription, with the provider owning the code, servers and updates. C (PaaS) supplies a development and runtime platform for building applications rather than ready-made ones. D (IaaS) rents raw compute, storage and networking, and B (DaaS) delivers hosted virtual desktops rather than individual productivity apps.

question: Which of the following is a way to synchronize the clocks across all devices in an environment?
explanation: An NTP server distributes time from an authoritative reference down a stratum hierarchy over UDP 123, keeping every client's clock in step, which matters for Kerberos authentication, certificate validity and readable logs. A (Shorter DHCP lease) only changes how often addresses renew. B (Public DNS) resolves names, and C (HTTP server) serves web content, neither of which touches system time.

question: Which of the following cable types requires a user to manually turn the connector in a clockwise direction in order to securely attach the cable?
explanation: Coaxial cable uses the F-type connector, whose threaded collar the user screws clockwise onto the jack until it is snug. A (Ethernet) uses an RJ45 with a plastic retention clip, and B (HDMI) relies on friction alone. C (Fiber-optic) LC and SC connectors push in and latch, and D (Serial) DB9 is secured by turning two separate thumbscrews rather than rotating the connector body.

question:
A technician installs a new workgroup MFP in a small office with a DHCP address. Immediately after the MFP is installed, office IoT devices using
 Wi-Fi experience connectivity issues. The office has a single Wi-Fi access point, and the IoT devices can only operate on the 2.4GHz spectrum.
 Which of the following should the technician do next to troubleshoot the issue?

options.A: Enable the Wi-Fi Direct feature on the MFP.
options.B: Configure the MFP with WPA3 instead of WPA2.
options.C: Connect the printer to the network using Ethernet.
options.D: Assign a unique static IP address.

explanation: The MFP joined the same crowded 2.4GHz band the IoT devices depend on, and its radio plus any built-in soft AP is congesting the single available channel; moving the printer onto wired Ethernet removes its transmissions from the air entirely. A (Enable Wi-Fi Direct) adds another 2.4GHz SSID and makes the interference worse. B (WPA3) is an encryption change, and D (Static IP) addresses address conflicts, neither of which affects radio congestion.

question:
A computer with two redundant drives is displaying an error:
 SMART failure predicted: Drive 1
 A technician notes that a spare drive is not available and the computer is currently functioning normally. Which of the following should the
 technician do next?
explanation: SMART is warning of a predicted failure, not an actual one, and the array is still redundant and working, so the right move is to source a replacement drive now and swap it during a planned window. A (Immediately remove the drive) drops redundancy with no spare on hand to rebuild onto. C (Rebuild the array) cannot happen until a new disk exists, and D (Restore the base image) is unnecessary because no data has been lost.

question:
Which of the following networking hardware devices is primarily used to connect different network segments and forward data based on MAC
 addresses?
explanation: A switch learns which MAC address lives behind each port and forwards frames only to that port, joining segments into one Layer 2 network without flooding traffic everywhere. A (Router) connects separate networks and forwards on IP addresses at Layer 3. C (Modem) converts signals between digital and the carrier's medium, and D (Firewall) permits or denies traffic based on rules, not on hardware addressing.

question:
An administrator is configuring a bare-metal server to host several virtual machines. Which of the following should the administrator use to
 complete this task?
explanation: A Type 1 hypervisor installs straight onto the bare-metal server and allocates its CPU, memory and storage to multiple virtual machines, which is exactly the described task. E (Container) runtimes still need a host operating system underneath and share its kernel. C (VDI) is a desktop delivery service built on top of virtualization, A (VLAN) is a network segmentation feature, and D (RDP) is a remote access protocol.

question: Which of the following is used to expose the wires in an unshielded twisted pair?
explanation: A cable stripper scores and removes the outer jacket without nicking the copper, exposing the twisted pairs for termination. C (Crimper) is what presses an RJ45 plug onto those conductors once they are exposed and ordered. B (Punchdown tool) seats individual wires into a 110 or 66 block and trims them, and A (Loopback plug) is a test device with no role in preparing cable.

question: Which of the following wireless technologies has the most range but is susceptible to more interference?
explanation: Wi-Fi 5 reaches tens of metres indoors, far beyond the other options, and it shares unlicensed spectrum with neighbouring networks, cordless devices, microwaves and Bluetooth, so it is the most interference-prone of the four. A (NFC) works at roughly four centimetres, and B (Bluetooth) covers about ten metres at Class 2. D (Infrared) needs unobstructed line of sight and is blocked by any object between the endpoints.

question:
A technician is setting up a SOHO router. The environment requires DHCP to be disabled. Which of the following address types must the
 technician configure?
explanation: With DHCP disabled, every host has to be given a manually assigned static address along with the subnet mask, default gateway and DNS servers, since nothing on the network will hand those out. B (Dynamic) is precisely what DHCP provides and is no longer available. D (APIPA) is a self-assigned 169.254 fallback that only reaches the local link, and C (Public) describes routability rather than assignment method.

question: A company's directory services server is located on premises. Which of the following best describes the directory services infrastructure?
explanation: Running directory services on hardware the company owns and operates in its own facility, dedicated to that single organization, is the definition of a private cloud deployment. C (Public cloud) means shared multi-tenant infrastructure owned by a provider. A (Hybrid cloud) requires both private and public components working together, and D (Community cloud) is infrastructure shared among several organizations with common requirements.

question:
After a technician installs a new network printer, the technician discovers that one of the printer features is not available. Which of the following
 should the technician do first?

options.D: Connect the printer with a USB cable.

explanation: New printers frequently ship with factory firmware that predates a feature, so flashing the current firmware is the quick, low-risk first step that often restores the missing capability along with other fixes. B (Contact the manufacturer) is premature before basic troubleshooting. C (Enable IPv6) has no bearing on device features, and D (Connect by USB) changes the connection method rather than enabling anything on the printer.

question:
A user’s monitor shows strange colored lines and flickers when adjusting the brightness. The user requires the device for daily professional tasks.
 Which of the following should a technician do to effectively address the screen issue, given cost and urgency considerations?

options.A: Suggest the user use a secondary monitor for essential tasks.
options.B: Conduct a factory reset to eliminate software issues
options.C: Install a screen protector to minimize flickering.
options.D: Check for loose connections on the display.

explanation: Coloured lines and flicker that react when the brightness is adjusted point at a marginal video or panel cable connection, and reseating it costs nothing and takes minutes, which fits the cost and urgency constraints. B (Factory reset) chases software when the symptoms are physical. C (Screen protector) does nothing for flicker, and A (Use a secondary monitor) is a workaround that leaves the fault in place.

question: Which of the following technologies uses smartphones to allow contactless entry to secure areas?
explanation: Near-field communication works over a few centimetres, which is why a phone held against a reader can present a stored credential for door access without any physical card. C (RFID) covers badge and fob systems but is not the technology a smartphone uses for this. D (Bluetooth) requires pairing and reaches much further, and B (IR) needs unobstructed line of sight.

question:
An administrator must configure a server that prioritizes data availability. Because the server will be accessed by many users, the administrator
 must also consider performance. Which of the following RAID levels best meets these requirements within a single array?
explanation: RAID 10 stripes across mirrored pairs, so reads and writes are spread over multiple spindles for performance while every block still has a full mirror, letting the array survive a drive loss in each pair. A (RAID 1) is redundant but gains no striping performance and gives only half the raw capacity. C (RAID 5) carries a parity write penalty and tolerates just one failure, and B (RAID 2) is obsolete and never deployed.

question:
An employee's corporate phone is experiencing connectivity issues. The user is unable to access the internet, send emails, or use business
 applications outside the office. The device is not in airplane mode, and Wi-Fi is turned off. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the
 issue?

options.A: The SIM is malfunctioning and needs to be replaced.
options.B: The user has exceeded the phone's mobile data plan.
options.D: The phone is missing security updates.

explanation: With Wi-Fi off, cellular data is the only path to the internet, so hitting the plan's cap and being cut off or throttled explains losing web, mail and business apps while the phone otherwise behaves normally. A (Malfunctioning SIM) would drop the carrier connection altogether, taking calls and texts with it. C (SSID settings) only apply to Wi-Fi, which is disabled, and D (Missing security updates) does not block data connectivity.

question: Which of the following display technologies is known for offering the highest contrast ratios?
explanation: OLED pixels emit their own light and switch completely off for black, so there is no light leakage and the contrast ratio is effectively infinite. A (LCD) and B (LED) both rely on a backlight that bleeds through the liquid crystal layer, so black renders as dark grey. D (QLED) is a quantum-dot enhanced LCD, which improves colour and brightness but is still backlit.

question:
A busy network printer is producing faded printouts after a technician performed maintenance on the printer several months ago. The technician
 now replaces the toner cartridge, but the issue persists. Which of the following should the technician check next?
explanation: With a fresh toner cartridge failing to fix the fading on a heavily used printer, the imaging drum is the next consumable in the path; once worn it no longer holds a uniform electrostatic charge, so it picks up less toner and output stays pale. A (Firmware) and D (Print resolution settings) would not have changed on their own months after the last maintenance, and B (Paper type) affects finish and quality rather than causing uniformly faint text.

question:
After several workstations received OS updates, users report that their network speeds have dropped. A technician verifies that the network
 speeds on other workstations are fine. Which of the following would most likely solve the issue on the updated workstations?

options.A: Rolling back to the previous driver

explanation: OS updates routinely replace network adapter drivers, and the slowdown appears only on the machines that were updated while everything else runs fine, so reverting to the previous driver in Device Manager restores the old behaviour. B (Replacing the network cards) throws hardware at a software regression. C (Restarting the router) would have to affect every workstation, not just the updated ones, and D (Switching to IPv6) does nothing about a driver problem.

question:
A user’s smartphone has stopped connecting to corporate Wi-Fi networks. The user has tried restarting the phone, but the issue persists. The
 device indicates full signal strength but fails to obtain an IP address during connection attempts. The user also notes that the smartphone can
 still connect to cellular data without any issues. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the connectivity issue?
explanation: Full signal means the phone associates with the access point fine, and failing at the address assignment stage points at DHCP, whether the server is down or its scope has run out of leases. C (Malfunctioning antenna) and D (Weak signal) are contradicted by the reported full signal strength and successful association. B (Outdated firmware) would not selectively break only address assignment while leaving cellular data working normally.

question:
A technician is migrating an application server to another server. Which of the following DNS records should the technician create to ensure
 seamless connectivity?
explanation: A CNAME aliases the application's existing hostname to the new server's name, so clients and shortcuts keep using the same address and resolution follows the service to its new home without touching every client. A (TXT) stores arbitrary text for verification purposes. B (SPF) and C (DKIM) are both published as TXT records for email authentication and have nothing to do with pointing users at a relocated application server.

question:
A company network is spread across multiple office branches that are located within the same postal code and connected using leased lines.
 Which of the following best describes this network type?
explanation: Several buildings clustered in one small geographic area, all within the same postal code and joined by the organization's own leased links, describes a campus area network. B (MAN) spans an entire city or metropolitan region, well beyond a single postal code. D (WAN) covers large geographic distances between distant sites, and C (LAN) is confined to a single building or floor.

question:
A user wants to use a new laptop to play audio and video to an office projector, but the laptop does not have VGA or HDMI. Which of the following
 adapters should the user buy?
explanation: USB-C supports DisplayPort Alternate Mode, so a USB-C to HDMI adapter carries both the video and the audio to the projector over one connection. C (DisplayPort to VGA) needs a DisplayPort output the laptop does not have, and VGA carries no audio at all. D (DVI to HDMI) likewise requires a DVI port, and DVI has no audio channel. B (MicroUSB to VGA) is not a video-capable path on a laptop.

question: Which of the following port numbers is used for NetBIOS?
explanation: B (137) is the NetBIOS Name Service port, part of the 137-139 NetBIOS range (137 name service, 138 datagram, 139 session). A (110) is POP3 for retrieving mail, and C (143) is IMAP, the other mail-retrieval protocol. D (445) is tempting because it carries SMB file sharing, but that is SMB directly over TCP, which replaced NetBIOS-based sharing rather than being NetBIOS itself.

question:
Which of the following describes a virtualization concept that improves resource utilization by allowing multiple operating systems to run on a
 single physical server?
explanation: B (Virtual machine) is the concept of a self-contained guest with its own virtual CPU, memory and disk, so several complete operating systems share one physical host and soak up otherwise idle capacity. C (Hypervisor) is the software layer that creates and schedules those VMs, not the concept being described. A (Containerization) shares the host's single kernel rather than running multiple OSes, and D (Microservices architecture) is an application design pattern.

question: Which of the following connector types would most likely be used to connect a fiber-optic cable to an SFP module?
explanation: D (LC) is the small form factor connector that SFP and SFP+ transceivers are built around, its compact duplex latch being exactly why high-density switch ports use it. B (SC) is the larger square push-pull connector found on patch panels and older gear. A (ST) is the round bayonet-twist connector from legacy multimode runs, and C (FC) is a threaded screw-on connector used where vibration is a concern. Neither fits an SFP cage.

question:
A developer needs to isolate a testing VM in a Type 1 hypervisor from the other guests. Which of the following does the administrator need to use
 to accomplish this task?
explanation: D (Sandbox) is an isolated execution environment that walls a test system off from other guests and the host, which is precisely what a developer needs before running untrusted or experimental code. B (Container) shares the host kernel and is not a guest under a Type 1 hypervisor, so it gives weaker isolation. A (VDI) is a way of delivering virtual desktops to users, and C (Private cloud) is a deployment model, not an isolation mechanism.

question:
A technician is building a custom CAD workstation with a high-end graphics card. The customer requests that the system has the highest possible
 stability. Which of the following is the best choice for the power supply?
explanation: B (Redundant) means two or more power supplies feed the system, so if one unit dies the other carries the load and the workstation keeps running. That directly answers a demand for maximum stability. A (UPS) protects against utility power loss but does nothing if the PSU itself fails. C (Surge protector) only clamps voltage spikes, and D (Modular) refers to detachable cabling for airflow and tidiness, which has no bearing on reliability.

question: Which of the following tools would most likely be used to identify a cable's location in the network closet?
explanation: C (Toner probe) is the tone generator and inductive probe pair: clip the tone onto a cable at one end, then sweep the probe across the bundle in the closet until it squeals over the matching run. A (Loopback plug) tests whether a port can transmit and receive, not where a cable terminates. B (Crimper) attaches connectors to cable ends, and D (Network tap) copies live traffic for capture and analysis.

question: Which of the following is the best option to maintain a stable, tethered connection between a cell phone and a laptop?
explanation: B (USB) tethering uses a physical cable, so the link cannot drift or drop from interference and the phone charges while it is connected, which is what makes it the most stable option. A (Bluetooth) tethering is far slower and susceptible to interference and range issues. C (Hotspot) is a wireless share, not a tether, and D (NFC) works only at a few centimetres and is meant for pairing and payments, not data throughput.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting a computer that fails to start and makes frequent, unexpected sounds. The monitor remains blank, and no OS
 loads. Which of the following should the technician review first to diagnose this issue?
explanation: D (Proper installation of RAM modules) is the first thing to check because repeated beeping with no video and no POST is the classic memory beep code, and a partially seated or failed DIMM stops the system before anything is displayed. A (Output voltages of power supplies) would more likely produce a dead machine with no fans or sounds at all. B (Thermal paste) causes overheating and shutdowns after boot, and C (OS boot configuration) cannot even be reached when POST never completes.

question: Which of the following contains details about its manufacturer and is hardcoded?
explanation: B (MAC) addresses are burned into the network adapter at the factory, and the first three bytes are the OUI that identifies the manufacturer, so the address is both hardcoded and vendor-revealing. D (IP) addresses are logical and assigned by DHCP or an administrator. C (APIPA) is a self-assigned 169.254.x.x address a host picks when DHCP fails, and A (DSL) is a broadband access technology, not an address.

question: Which of the following is used to implement PoE?
explanation: D (Injector) is the device that adds DC power onto an Ethernet run between a non-PoE switch and a powered device such as an access point or camera. That is the standard way to implement PoE without replacing the switch. C (Media converter) changes the physical medium, typically copper to fiber. B (Range extender) rebroadcasts a wireless signal, and A (Modem) modulates a signal for a broadband circuit. None of them supply power over the cable.

question:
A technician replaces a motherboard in a desktop computer. Alter reassembling the system and turning it on, the computer tails to start, and no
 display output is shown. The power supply fan and case fans are working, but there are no beep codes or POST messages. Which of the following
 should the technician do first to make the computer turn on properly?

options.A: Replace the power supply with a higher wattage unit.
options.B: Ensure that the CPU power connector is properly installed.

explanation: B (Ensure that the CPU power connector is properly installed) is the first check because the 4- or 8-pin EPS connector is the one most often forgotten during a board swap. Without it the board powers the fans but the CPU never initialises, so there is no POST, no beeps and no video. D (Reseat the memory modules) would normally still produce beep codes. A (Higher wattage PSU) is not indicated when fans already spin, and C (BIOS update) needs a machine that POSTs.

question: Which of the following devices can provide combined data and power to hardwired VoIP phones in a small office?
explanation: B (PoE switch) delivers both the network connection and 802.3af/at power on the same drop to every phone in the office from one device, which is the practical way to wire multiple VoIP handsets. A (Injector) also supplies PoE but only for a single run, so a small office would need one per phone. C (Optical network terminal) terminates a fiber service, and D (Router) forwards traffic between networks without energising the cable.

question:
A company requires a storage solution that combines performance and redundancy for a main database server with high levels of read/write
 operations. Which of the following storage configurations best meets these requirements?
explanation: D (RAID 10) stripes across mirrored pairs, so reads and writes are fast and any single drive in a mirror can fail without data loss. That combination of speed and redundancy suits a heavily used database. A (RAID 0) stripes for performance but has no fault tolerance at all. B (RAID 5) and C (RAID 6) carry a parity write penalty because every write recalculates parity, which hurts exactly the write-intensive workload described.

question: A user's laptop keyboard is distorted and is no longer flat. Which of the following components most likely tailed?
explanation: A (Battery) is the culprit: a lithium-ion pack that swells pushes upward against the chassis, bowing the keyboard and trackpad so the surface no longer sits flat. A swollen battery is a fire hazard and should be replaced immediately, never punctured. C (Keyboard) failure shows up as dead, stuck or repeating keys, not physical deformation. B (RAM) and D (HDD) faults present as crashes, boot errors or noise, and neither can distort the case.

question: Which of the following types of RAM is typically used in servers?
explanation: D (ECC) memory carries extra bits that let the controller detect and correct single-bit errors on the fly, which is why servers that must run for months without corrupting data use it. A (SODIMM) is the small form factor used in laptops and compact systems, not a reliability feature. C (DDR3) is simply a memory generation, and B (Rambus) is a long-obsolete standard that lost out to DDR.

question:
A specialist needs to configure a computer so that it will not boot up using any non-trusted or unsigned external devices that are connected to the
 computer. Which of the following should the specialist configure?
explanation: B (Secure Boot) is the UEFI feature that checks the digital signature of every bootloader and driver against a trusted database and refuses to hand off control to unsigned code, including anything on an attached external drive. A (BIOS password) stops someone changing firmware settings but never validates what boots. C (USB settings) can disable ports wholesale, which is blunt and does not address signing, and D (Single sign-on) governs application logins, not boot integrity.

question: Which of the following RAM characteristics allows for recovery from data faults in memory modules?
explanation: C (ECC) uses additional check bits so the memory controller can both spot and repair a single-bit error while the system keeps running, which is the recovery the question asks about. E (Parity) is the close contender, but a parity bit only flags that something changed, it carries no information to rebuild the correct value. A (Capacity), B (Speed) and D (DDR) describe how much memory there is and how fast it runs, not its error handling.
